title.zh: 卷一百五十三 志第一百〇六 輿服五
title.raw: 卷一百五十三 志第一百〇六 輿服五 Volume 153 Treatises 106: Carriages and Clothes 5

sentences.zh: 輿服五○諸臣服下士庶人服

translations.literal: Carriages and Clothes 5 ○ Dress of officials and ministers; dress of commoners and the people.
translations.idiomatic: Carriages and Clothes 5 — Official Dress; Dress of Commoners and the People

sentences.zh: 公服。

translations.literal: Official dress.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary Court Dress.

sentences.zh: 凡朝服謂之具服，公服從省，今謂之常服。

translations.literal: All court dress is called full dress; official dress is simplified; today it is called regular dress.
translations.idiomatic: Full court dress was called "complete dress"; ordinary court dress was a simplified form, and in the present day it is called regular dress.

sentences.zh: 宋因唐制，三品以上服紫，五品以上服朱，七品以上服綠，九品以上服青。

translations.literal: Song followed the Tang system: third rank and above wore purple, fifth rank and above wore vermillion, seventh rank and above wore green, ninth rank and above wore azure.
translations.idiomatic: The Song followed Tang practice: officials of the third rank and above wore purple, of the fifth rank and above vermillion, of the seventh rank and above green, and of the ninth rank and above azure.

sentences.zh: 其制，曲領大袖，下施橫襴，束以革帶，襆頭，烏皮靴。

translations.literal: Its form: curved collar, large sleeves, horizontal pleats below, bound with a leather belt, futou headwrap, and black leather boots.
translations.idiomatic: The garment had a curved collar and wide sleeves, horizontal pleats below the waist, a leather belt, a futou headwrap, and black leather boots.

sentences.zh: 自王公至一命之士，通服之。

translations.literal: From princes and dukes down to holders of the ninth rank, all wore it in common.
translations.idiomatic: From princes and dukes down to officials of the ninth rank, all wore it alike.

sentences.zh: 太宗太平興國二年，詔朝官出知節鎮及轉運使、副，衣緋、綠者並借紫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo under Emperor Taizong, an edict ordered that court officials sent out as commissioners of circuit commands and as transport commissioners or deputies, if wearing scarlet or green, might all borrow purple.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizong's second year of Taiping Xingguo (977), an edict allowed court officials assigned as circuit commissioners or transport commissioners (and their deputies) who wore scarlet or green to borrow purple robes.

sentences.zh: 知防禦、團練、刺史州，衣綠者借緋，衣緋者借紫；

translations.literal: For those governing defense, training, or prefectural states, wearers of green might borrow scarlet, and wearers of scarlet might borrow purple;
translations.idiomatic: Prefects of defense commands, training commands, and prefectural states who wore green could borrow scarlet, and those in scarlet could borrow purple;

sentences.zh: 其為通判、知軍監，止借緋。

translations.literal: those serving as deputy prefects or as supervisors of armies and agencies might borrow only scarlet.
translations.idiomatic: deputy prefects and army-or-agency supervisors were limited to borrowing scarlet.

sentences.zh: 其後，江淮發運使同轉運，提點刑獄同知刺史州。

translations.literal: Thereafter, the Jiang-Huai grain transport commissioner was treated like a transport commissioner, and the judicial intendant like a prefect of a prefectural state.
translations.idiomatic: Later, the Jiang-Huai grain transport commissioner received the same privileges as a transport commissioner, and the judicial intendant the same as a prefect.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，郊祀慶成，始許升朝官服緋、綠二十年者，敘賜緋、紫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi, when suburban sacrifices were completed in celebration, it was first permitted that court officials who had worn scarlet or green for twenty years receive graded bestowal of scarlet or purple.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongxi (984), after the suburban sacrifice celebrations, court officials who had worn scarlet or green for twenty years were first allowed to advance by seniority to scarlet or purple robes.

sentences.zh: 真宗登極，京朝官亦聽敘，及東封、西祀赦書，京朝官並以十五年為限。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong ascended the throne, capital court officials were also permitted advancement by seniority; in amnesties for the eastern and western sacrifices, capital court officials were all given a limit of fifteen years.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong took the throne, capital officials were also allowed seniority advancement; amnesties for the eastern and western sacrifices set a fifteen-year limit for capital officials.

sentences.zh: 後每帝登極，亦如例。

translations.literal: Thereafter, whenever an emperor ascended the throne, the precedent was likewise followed.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, each new emperor followed the same practice.

sentences.zh: 景德三年，詔內諸司使以下出入內庭，不得服皂衣，違者論其罪；

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingde, an edict ordered that commissioners of the inner bureaus and below, entering and leaving the inner court, must not wear black robes; violators were prosecuted;
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 3 (1006), an edict forbade inner-bureau commissioners and lower ranks from wearing black when entering the inner palace, on penalty of prosecution;

sentences.zh: 內職亦許服窄袍。

translations.literal: inner staff were also permitted to wear narrow-sleeved robes.
translations.idiomatic: inner staff were also allowed to wear narrow-sleeved robes.

sentences.zh: 仁宗景祐元年，詔軍使曾任通判者借緋，曾任知州者借紫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyou under Emperor Renzong, an edict ordered that military commissioners who had once served as deputy prefect might borrow scarlet, and those who had once served as prefect might borrow purple.
translations.idiomatic: In Renzong's first year of Jingyou (1034), military commissioners who had previously served as deputy prefect could borrow scarlet, and those who had served as prefect could borrow purple.

sentences.zh: 慶曆元年，龍圖閣直學士任布言：「欲望自今贈官至正郎者，其畫像許服緋，至卿監許服紫。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingli, Academician-Expositor Ren Bu of the Dragon Diagram Hall said: "It is desired that from now on, for posthumous enfeoffment up to Regular Gentleman, their portraits be permitted to wear scarlet, and up to director of a directorate, purple dress."
translations.idiomatic: In Qingli 1 (1041), Dragon Diagram Hall academician Ren Bu proposed: "Henceforth, for posthumous honors up to Regular Gentleman, portraits should be allowed scarlet robes, and up to director rank, purple robes."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐三年，詔三路轉運使朝辭上殿日，與賜章服；

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiayou, an edict ordered that when transport commissioners of the three circuits took leave at court on the day of their audience, they were to be bestowed court regalia;
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou 3 (1058), transport commissioners of the three circuits were to receive court regalia on the day they took leave at audience;

sentences.zh: 諸路轉運使候及十年，即與賜章服。

translations.literal: transport commissioners of all circuits, once they had waited ten years, were likewise bestowed court regalia.
translations.idiomatic: transport commissioners in all circuits received regalia after ten years of service.

sentences.zh: 徽宗重和元年，詔禮制局自冠服討論以聞，其見服靴，先改用履。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chonghe under Emperor Huizong, an edict ordered the Ritual Regulations Bureau to deliberate on caps and dress and report; for present dress, boots were first to be changed to shoes.
translations.idiomatic: In Huizong's first year of Chonghe (1118), the Ritual Regulations Bureau was ordered to review caps and dress; boots in current use were to be replaced first with court shoes.

sentences.zh: 禮制局奏：「履有絇、繶、純、綦，古者舄履各隨裳之色，有赤舄、白舄、黑舄。

translations.literal: The Ritual Regulations Bureau memorialized: "Shoes have laces, side ornaments, borders, and ties; in antiquity shoes and slippers each followed the color of the lower garment, with red slippers, white slippers, and black slippers.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau reported: "Court shoes had laces, side ornaments, borders, and ties. In antiquity, shoes matched the color of the skirt—red, white, or black slippers.

sentences.zh: 今履欲用黑革為之，其絇、繶、純、綦並隨服色用之，以仿古隨裳色之意。」

translations.literal: Now it is desired that shoes be made of black leather, and that laces, side ornaments, borders, and ties all follow the color of the dress, to imitate the ancient meaning of following garment color."
translations.idiomatic: Shoes should be black leather, with laces and ornaments matching robe color, reviving the ancient practice of coordinating footwear with dress."

sentences.zh: 詔以明年正旦改用。

translations.literal: An edict ordered adoption from the New Year's audience of the following year.
translations.idiomatic: The change was ordered for the next New Year's audience.

sentences.zh: 禮制局又言：「履隨其服色。

translations.literal: The Ritual Regulations Bureau again said: "Shoes follow the color of the dress.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau added: "Shoes should match robe color.

sentences.zh: 武臣服色一等，當議差別。」

translations.literal: Military officials' dress colors are of one grade; distinctions ought to be deliberated."
translations.idiomatic: Military officials shared one color grade; distinctions should be discussed."

sentences.zh: 詔文武官大夫以上具四飾，朝請郎、武功郎以下去繶，並稱履；

translations.literal: An edict ordered that civil and military officials of Grandee and above have all four ornaments; Court Gentleman for Court Consultation, Martial Achievement Gentleman, and below remove side ornaments, and all are called shoes;
translations.idiomatic: Grandees and above kept all four ornaments; Court Gentlemen and Martial Achievement Gentlemen and below dropped side ornaments—all were called shoes;

sentences.zh: 從義郎、宣教郎以下至將校、伎術官去繶、純，並稱履。

translations.literal: Gentlemen for Following Righteousness, Gentlemen for Promoting Instruction, and below down to commanders and technical officers removed side ornaments and borders, and all were called shoes.
translations.idiomatic: From Following Righteousness and Promoting Instruction Gentlemen down to commanders and technical officers, side ornaments and borders were removed—all wore shoes.

sentences.zh: 當時議者以靴不當用之中國，實廢釋氏之漸雲。

translations.literal: Commentators of the time held that boots were unsuitable for use in China and that this was in truth a gradual abolition of Buddhist custom.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries argued that boots were inappropriate in China and that the reform was really a step toward abandoning Buddhist dress.

sentences.zh: 中興，仍元豐之制，四品以上紫，六品以上緋，九品以上綠。

translations.literal: At the Restoration, the Yuanfeng system was retained: fourth rank and above purple, sixth rank and above scarlet, ninth rank and above green.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration, the Yuanfeng rules remained: fourth rank and above wore purple, sixth rank and above scarlet, ninth rank and above green.

sentences.zh: 服緋、紫者必佩魚，謂之章服。

translations.literal: Wearers of scarlet and purple must wear the fish tally; this is called court regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Scarlet and purple robes required a fish tally and were called court regalia.

sentences.zh: 非官至本品，不以假人。

translations.literal: Unless one has reached office of one's proper rank, it is not lent to others.
translations.idiomatic: Robes were not loaned unless one held the corresponding rank.

sentences.zh: 若官卑而職高，則特許者有三：自庶官遷六部侍郎，自庶官為待制，或出奉使者是也。

translations.literal: If rank is low but office is high, there are three special permissions: promotion from common official to vice minister of a Six Ministry, from common official to academician-in-waiting, or service as an envoy on imperial commission.
translations.idiomatic: When rank was low but office high, three exceptions applied: promotion from common official to vice minister, appointment as academician-in-waiting, or service as an imperial envoy.

sentences.zh: 又有以年勞而賜者，有品未及而借者。

translations.literal: There were also those bestowed for years of service, and those who borrowed because rank had not yet been reached.
translations.idiomatic: Some received robes for seniority; others borrowed them before reaching the proper rank.

sentences.zh: 升朝官服綠，大夫以上服緋，蒞事至今日以前及二十年曆任無過者，許磨勘改授章服，此賜者也。

translations.literal: Court officials wore green; grandees and above wore scarlet; those who had held office to the present day and before, with twenty years of service without fault, were permitted review and reassignment of court regalia—this was bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials wore green; grandees and above wore scarlet. After twenty years of faultless service, review could advance one's regalia—this was bestowal by seniority.

sentences.zh: 或為通判者，許借緋；

translations.literal: those serving as deputy prefect were permitted to borrow scarlet;
translations.idiomatic: deputy prefects could borrow scarlet;

sentences.zh: 為知州、監司者，許借紫；

translations.literal: those serving as prefect or supervisory commissioner were permitted to borrow purple;
translations.idiomatic: prefects and supervisory commissioners could borrow purple;

sentences.zh: 任滿還朝，仍服本品，此借者也。

translations.literal: when terms ended and they returned to court, they still wore their proper rank—this was borrowing.
translations.idiomatic: on returning to court after a term, they resumed their proper rank—this was borrowing.

sentences.zh: 又有出於恩賜者焉。

translations.literal: There were also those arising from gracious bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: Some robes came as special imperial favors.

sentences.zh: 紹興十二年九月，以皇太后回鑾，詔承務郎以上服緋、綠，蒞事至今日以前十七年者，並改轉服色。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twelfth year of Shaoxing, because the Empress Dowager returned to the imperial carriage, an edict ordered that Gentlemen for Supporting Affairs and above who wore scarlet or green, with office held to the present day and before for seventeen years, all had their dress colors changed by advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 12/9 (1142), celebrating the Empress Dowager's return, Gentlemen for Supporting Affairs and above in scarlet or green with seventeen years of service were advanced in robe color.

sentences.zh: 三十二年六月，孝宗即位，詔承務郎以上服緋、綠及十五年者，並許改轉服色。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the thirty-second year, when Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne, an edict ordered that Gentlemen for Supporting Affairs and above who wore scarlet or green for fifteen years were all permitted to change their dress colors by advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year 32 (1165), when Xiaozong took the throne, Supporting Affairs Gentlemen and above with fifteen years in scarlet or green could advance their robe color.

sentences.zh: 然計年之法，亦不輕許。

translations.literal: Yet the method of counting years was not lightly granted.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, seniority rules were applied strictly.

sentences.zh: 無出身人自年二十出官服綠日起理，服緋人亦自年二十服緋日起理，有出身人自賜出身日起理；

translations.literal: Those without examination pedigree counted from age twenty when they first took office wearing green; scarlet wearers also counted from age twenty when they first wore scarlet; those with pedigree counted from the day of bestowed pedigree;
translations.idiomatic: Men without examination degrees counted from age twenty when they first wore green in office; scarlet wearers from age twenty in scarlet; degree holders from the day their degree was conferred;

sentences.zh: 內並除豁丁憂年、月、日不理外，曆任無過者方許焉。

translations.literal: within this, excepting years, months, and days of mourning for parents not counted, only those with service records without fault were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: mourning years were excluded, and only officials with faultless records qualified.

sentences.zh: 先是，殿中侍御史張震奏：「今日之弊，在於人有僥幸。

translations.literal: Earlier, Palace Attendant Censor Zhang Zhen memorialized: "Today's abuse lies in people's taking lucky chances.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Palace Attendant Censor Zhang Zhen warned: "Today's abuse is opportunism.

sentences.zh: 能革其俗，然後天下可治。

translations.literal: If this custom can be reformed, then All Under Heaven can be governed.
translations.idiomatic: Reform that habit, and the realm can be governed.

sentences.zh: 且改轉服色，常赦自升朝官以上服綠，大夫以上服緋，蒞事及二十年，方得改賜。

translations.literal: Moreover, for changing dress colors, in ordinary amnesties court officials and above who wore green, and grandees and above who wore scarlet, required twenty years of holding office before they could receive changed bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary amnesties required court officials in green and grandees in scarlet to serve twenty years before advancing robe color.

sentences.zh: 今赦日承務郎以上服緋、綠及十五年，便與改轉。

translations.literal: Now on amnesty day, Gentlemen for Supporting Affairs and above who wore scarlet or green for fifteen years are at once given advancement.
translations.idiomatic: This amnesty advanced Supporting Affairs Gentlemen and above in scarlet or green after only fifteen years.

sentences.zh: 比之常赦，不惟年限已減，而又官品相絕，蓋已為異恩矣。

translations.literal: Compared with ordinary amnesties, not only has the term been reduced, but official ranks are utterly different—this is already a special grace.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with ordinary amnesties, the term was shorter and the ranks eligible far lower—already an extraordinary favor.

sentences.zh: 今竊聞省、部欲自補官日便理歲月，即是嬰孩授命，年才十五者今遂服緋；

translations.literal: Now it is privately heard that the ministries wish to count years from the day of initial appointment, so that an infant receiving appointment—a youth of only fifteen—would now wear scarlet;
translations.idiomatic: I hear the ministries want to count from the day of initial appointment, so a youth of fifteen could wear scarlet;

sentences.zh: 而貴近之子，或初年賜緋，年才及冠者今遂賜紫。

translations.literal: while sons of the noble and intimate, some bestowed scarlet in their first year, youths barely of capping age would now be bestowed purple.
translations.idiomatic: and sons of the powerful, scarlet in their first year, could receive purple before they were even twenty.

sentences.zh: 朱、紫紛紛，不亦濫乎？

translations.literal: Vermillion and purple in profusion—is this not excessive?
translations.idiomatic: Vermillion and purple everywhere—is that not abuse?

sentences.zh: 況靖康、建炎恩赦，亦不曾以補官日為始。

translations.literal: Moreover, amnesties of Jingkang and Jianyan never began counting from the day of initial appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Jingkang and Jianyan amnesties did not count from initial appointment.

sentences.zh: 若始於出官之日，頗為折衷，蓋比之蒞事所減已多，而比之初補粗為有節。」

translations.literal: If counting began from the day of taking office, that would be a fair compromise, for compared with holding office it is already much reduced, yet compared with initial appointment it still has some restraint."
translations.idiomatic: Counting from the day one took office would be a compromise—less generous than counting full service, yet stricter than counting from initial appointment."

sentences.zh: 帝從其言，故有是命。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed his words; hence this order.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted this advice, hence the order on counting years.

sentences.zh: 又有出於特賜者，旌直臣則賜之，勸循吏則賜之，廣孝治則賜之，優老臣則賜之，此皆非常制焉。

translations.literal: There were also those arising from special bestowal: upright ministers were bestowed it, diligent local officials were bestowed it, filial governance was extended by bestowing it, aged ministers were honored by bestowing it—these were all outside the regular system.
translations.idiomatic: Special bestowals honored upright ministers, encouraged diligent local officials, extended filial governance, and favored aged ministers—all outside the regular rules.

sentences.zh: 內品未至而賜服及借者，並於銜內帶賜及借。

translations.literal: Those within whose rank had not been reached yet who were bestowed dress or borrowed it all carried "bestowed" or "borrowed" in their titles.
translations.idiomatic: When rank had not been reached, bestowed or borrowed robes were marked as such in the official title.

sentences.zh: 襆頭。

translations.literal: Futou headwrap.
translations.idiomatic: The Futou Headwrap.

sentences.zh: 一名折上巾，起自後周，然止以軟帛垂腳，隋始以桐木為之，唐始以羅代繒。

translations.literal: Also called the folded-up kerchief; it arose in Later Zhou, but at first used only soft silk with hanging flaps; Sui first made it of paulownia wood; Tang first used gauze in place of heavy silk.
translations.idiomatic: Also called the "folded-up kerchief," it began in Later Zhou with soft silk flaps; Sui used paulownia wood, and Tang replaced heavy silk with gauze.

sentences.zh: 惟帝服則腳上曲，人臣下垂。

translations.literal: Only the emperor's dress had flaps curving upward; ministers' hung down.
translations.idiomatic: Only the emperor's flaps curved upward; ministers' hung straight down.

sentences.zh: 五代漸變平直。

translations.literal: In the Five Dynasties it gradually became straight and flat.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Five Dynasties the flaps gradually became straight.

sentences.zh: 國朝之制，君臣通服平腳，乘輿或服上曲焉。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's system: ruler and ministers alike wear flat flaps; the imperial carriage sometimes wears upward-curving ones.
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty, ruler and ministers alike wear flat flaps; only the emperor sometimes wears upward-curving ones.

sentences.zh: 其初以藤織草巾子為裏，紗為表，而塗以漆。

translations.literal: At first rattan-woven grass-cloth caps were used as lining, gauze as surface, and lacquer was applied.
translations.idiomatic: At first the frame was rattan and grass-cloth lined, gauze surfaced, and lacquered.

sentences.zh: 後惟以漆為堅，去其藤裏，前為一折，平施兩腳，以鐵為之。

translations.literal: Later only lacquer was used for firmness; the rattan lining was removed; the front had one fold; two flaps were set flat; iron was used to make them.
translations.idiomatic: Later only lacquer stiffened the cap; the rattan lining was dropped; the front was folded once, two flat iron flaps attached.

sentences.zh: 帶。

translations.literal: Belts.
translations.idiomatic: Belts.

sentences.zh: 古惟用革，自曹魏而下，始有金、銀、銅之飾。

translations.literal: In antiquity only leather was used; from Cao-Wei and below, gold, silver, and copper ornaments first appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient belts were leather only; from Cao Wei onward, gold, silver, and copper ornaments appeared.

sentences.zh: 宋制尤詳，有玉、有金、有銀、有犀，其下銅、鐵、角、石、墨玉之類，各有等差。

translations.literal: Song regulations were especially detailed: there were jade, gold, silver, and rhinoceros; below these copper, iron, horn, stone, dark jade, and the like, each with its grades.
translations.idiomatic: Song regulations were especially detailed: jade, gold, silver, and rhinoceros horn belts, and below them copper, iron, horn, stone, and dark jade, each with graded restrictions.

sentences.zh: 玉帶不許施於公服。

translations.literal: Jade belts were not permitted on official dress.
translations.idiomatic: Jade belts were not worn with ordinary court dress.

sentences.zh: 犀非品官、通犀非特旨皆禁。

translations.literal: Rhinoceros [belts] for non-ranked officials, and full rhinoceros without special edict, were all forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Rhinoceros belts were forbidden to unranked officials, and full rhinoceros belts without special edict.

sentences.zh: 銅、鐵、角、石、墨玉之類，民庶及郡縣吏、伎術等人，皆得服之。

translations.literal: Copper, iron, horn, stone, dark jade, and the like—commoners, commandery and county clerks, technical officers, and such might all wear them.
translations.idiomatic: Copper, iron, horn, stone, and dark jade belts were permitted to commoners, local clerks, and technical officers.

sentences.zh: 其制有金球路、荔支、師蠻、海捷、寶藏，

translations.literal: Its types included gold Ball-Road, Lychee, Teacher-Barbarian, Sea-Victory, and Treasure-Store,
translations.idiomatic: Gold belt plaques included Ball-Road, Lychee, Teacher-Barbarian, Sea-Victory, and Treasure-Store,

sentences.zh: 〈（方團二十五兩；

translations.literal: (square-round, twenty-five taels;
translations.idiomatic: square-round plaques, twenty-five taels;

sentences.zh: 荔支自二十五兩至七兩，有四等；

translations.literal: lychee from twenty-five taels down to seven taels, in four grades;
translations.idiomatic: lychee from twenty-five to seven taels in four grades;

sentences.zh: 師蠻二十五兩；

translations.literal: Teacher-Barbarian twenty-five taels;
translations.idiomatic: Teacher-Barbarian, twenty-five taels;

sentences.zh: 海捷十五兩；

translations.literal: Sea-Victory fifteen taels;
translations.idiomatic: Sea-Victory, fifteen taels;

sentences.zh: 寶藏三十兩。

translations.literal: Treasure-Store thirty taels.
translations.idiomatic: Treasure-Store, thirty taels.

sentences.zh: 惟球路方團胯，餘悉方胯。

translations.literal: Only Ball-Road had square-round plaques; the rest were all square plaques.

sentences.zh: 太宗太平興國七年正月，翰林學士承旨李昉等奏曰：「奉詔詳定車服制度，請從三品以上服玉帶，四品以上服金帶，以下升朝官、雖未升朝已賜紫緋、內職諸軍將校，並服紅鞓金塗銀排方。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo under Emperor Taizong, Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Li Fang and others memorialized: "By edict we have examined and fixed carriage and dress regulations. We request that third rank and above wear jade belts, fourth rank and above wear gold belts, and below them court officials, those not yet court officials but already bestowed purple or scarlet, inner staff, and army commanders and officers all wear red-strapped gilt-silver square plaques.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizong's seventh year of Taiping Xingguo (982), Hanlin chief Li Fang reported: "By edict we have set carriage and dress rules. Third rank and above should wear jade belts, fourth rank and above gold belts, and court officials, those granted purple or scarlet before promotion, inner staff, and military officers should wear red-strapped gilt-silver square plaques.

sentences.zh: 雖升朝著綠者，公服上不得係銀帶，餘官服黑銀方團胯及犀角帶。

translations.literal: Although court officials wearing green might not fasten silver belts on official dress, other officials wore black-silver square-round plaques and rhinoceros-horn belts.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials in green could not wear silver belts with ordinary dress; other officials wore black-silver square plaques or rhinoceros belts.

sentences.zh: 貢士及胥吏、工商、庶人服鐵角帶，恩賜者不用此制。

translations.literal: Presented scholars, clerks, artisans, merchants, and commoners wore iron and horn belts; those with gracious bestowal did not use this system.
translations.idiomatic: Exam candidates, clerks, artisans, merchants, and commoners wore iron and horn belts; those with special grants were exempt.

sentences.zh: 荔支帶本是內出以賜將相，在於庶僚，豈合僭服？

translations.literal: Lychee belts were originally issued from within to bestow on chief ministers and generals; how could subordinate officials presumptuously wear them?
translations.idiomatic: Lychee belts were issued from the palace for chief ministers and generals—how could junior officials wear them?

sentences.zh: 望非恩賜者，官至三品乃得服之。」

translations.literal: It is hoped that without gracious bestowal, one must reach third rank before being permitted to wear them."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that without special grant, only third rank and above may wear them."

sentences.zh: 景德三年，詔通犀、金、玉帶，除官品合服及恩賜外，餘人不得服用。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingde, an edict ordered that full rhinoceros, gold, and jade belts, except where rank permitted or gracious bestowal applied, might not be worn by others.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 3 (1006), full rhinoceros, gold, and jade belts were forbidden except by rank or special grant.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符五年，詔曰：「方團金帶，優寵輔臣，今文武庶官及伎術之流，率以金銀仿效，甚紊彝製。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, an edict said: "Square-round gold belts favor chief ministers; now civil and military common officials and technical classes all imitate them in gold and silver, greatly disordering the regular system.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 5 (1012), an edict declared: "Square gold belts honor chief ministers, yet civil and military officials and technical officers now copy them in gold and silver, disordering proper regulations.

sentences.zh: 自今除恩賜外，悉禁之。」

translations.literal: From now on, except for gracious bestowal, all are forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth all such imitation is forbidden except by special grant."

sentences.zh: 端拱中，詔作瑞草地球路文方團胯帶，副以金魚，賜中書、樞密院文臣。

translations.literal: In the Duan-Gong period, an edict ordered making square-round plaque belts with auspicious-grass and earth Ball-Road patterns, with gold fish attached, bestowed on civil officials of the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Duan-Gong (988–989), square belts with auspicious-grass and Ball-Road patterns and gold fish tally were made for Secretariat and Military Affairs civil officials.

sentences.zh: 仁宗慶曆八年，彰信軍節度使兼侍中李用和言：「伏見張耆授兼侍中日，特賜笏頭金帶以為榮異，欲望正謝日，準例特賜。」

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Qingli under Emperor Renzong, Military Commissioner of Zhangxin Army and Concurrent Palace Attendant Li Yonghe said: "I observe that on the day Zhang Qi received concurrent Palace Attendant, he was specially bestowed a tablet-head gold belt as a mark of honor. I desire that on the day of formal thanks, I receive a special bestowal by precedent."
translations.idiomatic: In Renzong's Qingli 8 (1048), Li Yonghe, commissioner of Zhangxin and concurrent palace attendant, noted that Zhang Qi had received a tablet-head gold belt when appointed attendant and asked for the same honor at his thanksgiving audience."

sentences.zh: 詔如耆例。

translations.literal: An edict followed Qi's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The court followed Qi's precedent.

sentences.zh: 神宗熙寧六年，熙河路奏捷，宰臣王安石率群臣賀紫宸殿，神宗解所服白玉帶賜之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xining under Emperor Shenzong, the Xihe circuit reported victory; Chief Minister Wang Anshi led the host of ministers to congratulate at the Zichen Hall; Shenzong removed the white jade belt he wore and bestowed it.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenzong's Xining 6 (1073), after the Xihe victory report, Wang Anshi led the ministers to congratulate at the Zichen Hall, and Shenzong gave him the white jade belt from his own waist.

sentences.zh: 八年，岐王顥、嘉王頵言：「蒙賜方團玉帶，著為朝儀，乞寶藏於家，不敢服用。」

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Prince of Qi Hao and Prince of Jia Yun said: "We have received bestowal of square-round jade belts, established as court ritual. We beg to treasure them at home and dare not wear them."
translations.idiomatic: In year 8, Princes Hao of Qi and Yun of Jia said: "We were granted square jade belts as court regalia but beg to keep them at home and not wear them."

sentences.zh: 神宗不許，命工別琢玉帶以賜之。

translations.literal: Shenzong did not permit it and ordered craftsmen to carve separate jade belts to bestow on them.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong refused and had separate jade belts carved for them.

sentences.zh: 顥等固辭，不聽；

translations.literal: Hao and the others firmly declined, but he would not listen;
translations.idiomatic: They declined again, but he would not hear of it;

sentences.zh: 請加佩金魚以別嫌，詔以玉魚賜之。

translations.literal: they requested adding gold fish to distinguish suspicion; an edict bestowed jade fish on them.
translations.idiomatic: they asked to wear gold fish to avoid suspicion, and an edict granted them jade fish instead.

sentences.zh: 親王佩玉魚自此始。

translations.literal: Imperial princes wearing jade fish began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes wearing jade fish tally began here.

sentences.zh: 宗旦、宗諤皆以使相遇郊恩告謝，特賜球文方團金帶、佩魚，自是宗室節度帶同平章事者，著為例。

translations.literal: Zongdan and Zong'e, both on meeting the envoy at suburban grace and offering thanks, were specially bestowed Ball-pattern square-round gold belts and fish tally; from this, imperial clansmen who were military commissioners with concurrent Grand Councilor became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Zongdan and Zong'e, on meeting envoys at suburban amnesty audiences, received Ball-pattern gold belts and fish tally; thereafter this became precedent for imperial clansmen who were commissioners with Grand Councilor rank.

sentences.zh: 宣徽使張方平、郭逵、王拱辰皆嘗特賜。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Commissioners Zhang Fangping, Guo Kui, and Wang Gongchen had all received special bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: Palace commissioners Zhang Fangping, Guo Kui, and Wang Gongchen had all received such special grants.

sentences.zh: 元豐五年，詔：「三師、三公、宰相、執政官、開府儀同三司、節度使嘗任宰相者、觀文殿大學士已上，金球文方團帶，佩魚。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng, an edict ordered: "Grand Preceptor, Grand Mentor, Grand Guardian, Three Dukes, Chancellor, Participating Officials, Grandee of Splendid Happiness with Equal Third Rank, military commissioners who had once served as chancellor, and Academicians of the Hall for Viewing Literature and above—gold Ball-pattern square-round belts, wearing fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng (1082), an edict fixed: "Grand preceptors, three dukes, chancellors, participating officials, honorary grandees, former chancellors serving as commissioners, and Viewing Literature grand academicians and above wore gold Ball-pattern belts with fish tally.

sentences.zh: 觀文殿學士至寶文閣直學士、節度使、御史大夫、中丞、六曹尚書、侍郎、散騎常侍御仙花帶，內御史大夫、六曹尚書、翰林學士以上及資政殿學士特班翰林學士上者，仍佩魚。」

translations.literal: Academicians of the Hall for Viewing Literature down to Expositors of the Hall for Treasuring Literature, military commissioners, Censor-in-Chief, Vice Censor-in-Chief, Six Ministries directors, vice ministers, and Regular Attendant—Immortal Flower belts; among them Censor-in-Chief, Six Ministries directors, Hanlin academicians and above, and Policy Council academicians specially ranked above Hanlin academicians still wore fish tally."
translations.idiomatic: Viewing Literature academicians through Treasuring Literature expositor-rank, commissioners, censors-in-chief and vice, ministry directors and vice ministers, and regular attendants wore Immortal Flower belts; censors-in-chief, ministry directors, Hanlin academicians and above, and Policy Council academicians ranked above Hanlin still wore fish tally."

sentences.zh: 六年，詔：「北使經過處，守臣曾借朝議大夫者，令權服紫，不係金帶。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict ordered: "Where northern envoys passed, defending officials who had borrowed Grandee for Court Discussion might temporarily wear purple and not fasten gold belts.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6, where northern envoys passed, officials who had borrowed Grandee for Court Discussion rank could temporarily wear purple without gold belts.

sentences.zh: 其押賜御筵官仍互借，先借朝議大夫者，即借中散大夫，並許係金帶，不佩魚。」

translations.literal: Officials escorting imperial banquets still borrowed from one another; those who first borrowed Grandee for Court Discussion then borrowed Grandee for Palace Attendance, all permitted to fasten gold belts but not wear fish tally."
translations.idiomatic: Banquet escorts could borrow ranks from one another—Court Discussion grandee, then Palace Attendance grandee—with gold belts but no fish tally."

sentences.zh: 哲宗元祐五年，詔：臣僚曾賜金帶後至不該係者，在外許係。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanyou under Emperor Zhezong, an edict ordered: officials once bestowed gold belts who later did not qualify to fasten them were permitted to fasten them when outside [the capital].
translations.idiomatic: In Zhezong's Yuanyou 5 (1090), officials once granted gold belts who no longer qualified by rank could still wear them outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 徽宗崇寧二年，詔：六尚局奉御，今後許服金帶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongning under Emperor Huizong, an edict ordered: attendants of the Six Bureaus of the Inner Service might henceforth wear gold belts.
translations.idiomatic: In Huizong's Chongning 2 (1103), attendants of the Six Inner Bureaus were allowed to wear gold belts.

sentences.zh: 四年，中書省檢會哲宗《元符儀製令》：「諸帶，三師、三公、宰相、執政官、使相、節度使、觀文殿大學士球文，佩魚。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Secretariat collated Zhezong's Yuanfu Ritual Regulations: "For all belts, Grand Preceptor, Three Dukes, Chancellor, Participating Officials, envoy-chancellors, military commissioners, and Viewing Literature grand academicians—Ball pattern, wearing fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, the Secretariat reviewed Zhezong's Yuanfu ritual code: "Grand preceptors, three dukes, chancellors, participating officials, envoy-chancellors, commissioners, and Viewing Literature grand academicians wore Ball-pattern belts with fish tally.

sentences.zh: 節度使非曾任宰相即禦仙花，佩魚。

translations.literal: Military commissioners who had not once served as chancellor wore Immortal Flower and fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners who had not been chancellor wore Immortal Flower belts with fish tally.

sentences.zh: 觀文殿學士至寶文閣直學士、御史大夫、中丞、六曹尚書、侍郎、散騎常侍並禦仙花，權侍郎不同；

translations.literal: Viewing Literature academicians down to Treasuring Literature expositor-rank, Censor-in-Chief, Vice Censor-in-Chief, Six Ministries directors, vice ministers, and Regular Attendant all wore Immortal Flower; acting vice ministers were different;
translations.idiomatic: Viewing Literature academicians through Treasuring Literature expositor-rank, censors, ministry directors and vice ministers, and regular attendants wore Immortal Flower belts; acting vice ministers did not;

sentences.zh: 內御史大夫、六曹尚書、觀文殿學士至翰林學士仍佩魚，資政殿學士特旨班在翰林學士上者同，權尚書不同。

translations.literal: among them Censor-in-Chief, Six Ministries directors, Viewing Literature academicians down to Hanlin academicians still wore fish tally; Policy Council academicians specially ranked above Hanlin academicians were the same; acting directors were different.
translations.idiomatic: among these, censors-in-chief, ministry directors, Viewing Literature academicians through Hanlin, and Policy Council academicians ranked above Hanlin still wore fish tally; acting directors did not.

sentences.zh: 其官職未至而特賜者，不拘此令。

translations.literal: Those whose offices had not been reached but who received special bestowal were not bound by this regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Special grants were not bound by these rules.

sentences.zh: 因任職事官經賜金帶者，雖後任不該賜，亦許服。」

translations.literal: Those who while serving in substantive office had been bestowed gold belts, though later appointments did not qualify for bestowal, were still permitted to wear them."
translations.idiomatic: Officials granted gold belts while holding substantive office could continue to wear them even if later posts did not qualify."

sentences.zh: 看詳：若稱因任六曹侍郎經賜帶，後除知開封府之類，既非職事官，又非在外，皆不許係，似非元立法之意。

translations.literal: Review: if one claims that because while serving as Six Ministries vice minister one was bestowed a belt, then after appointment as prefect of Kaifeng and the like—being neither substantive office nor outside—one may not fasten it, this seems not the original legislative intent.
translations.idiomatic: Review noted: if a vice minister granted a belt later became Kaifeng prefect—a post neither substantive nor outside the capital—he could not wear it, which seemed contrary to the original law.

sentences.zh: 蓋立文該舉未盡，其特賜者既不緣官職，自無時不許係外；

translations.literal: The drafting text did not cover all cases exhaustively. Special bestowals, not tied to office, were never restricted outside the capital;
translations.idiomatic: The text was incomplete. Special grants, not tied to office, were always permitted outside the capital;

sentences.zh: 因任職事官賜金帶，後任不該者亦許服，即在外與在京非職事官，皆可用。

translations.literal: gold belts bestowed while in substantive office might still be worn when later appointments did not qualify—both outside and in the capital for non-substantive offices, all might be used.
translations.idiomatic: belts granted in substantive office could still be worn in later posts that did not qualify, whether in the capital or outside.

sentences.zh: 詔申明行下。

translations.literal: An edict clarified and promulgated this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict clarified and circulated the rule.

sentences.zh: 大觀二年，詔中書舍人、諫議大夫、待制、殿中少監許係紅鞓犀帶，不佩魚。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daguan, an edict permitted Secretariat Drafters, Remonstrance Grandees, academicians-in-waiting, and Palace Vice Directors to fasten red-strapped rhinoceros belts without wearing fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: In Daguan 2 (1108), Secretariat drafters, remonstrance grandees, academicians-in-waiting, and palace vice directors could wear red-strapped rhinoceros belts without fish tally.

sentences.zh: 中興仍之，其等亦有玉、有金、有銀、有金塗銀、有犀、有通犀、有角。

translations.literal: At the Restoration this continued; the grades also had jade, gold, silver, gilt silver, rhinoceros, full rhinoceros, and horn.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration these rules continued, with jade, gold, silver, gilt silver, rhinoceros, full rhinoceros, and horn belts.

sentences.zh: 其制，球文者四方五團，禦仙花者排方。

translations.literal: Its form: Ball pattern had five roundels on four sides; Immortal Flower had square plaques in a row.
translations.idiomatic: Ball-pattern belts had five roundels on four sides; Immortal Flower belts used a row of square plaques.

sentences.zh: 凡金帶：三公、左右丞相、三少、使相、執政官、觀文殿大學士、節度使球文，佩魚；

translations.literal: For all gold belts: Three Dukes, Left and Right Chancellors, Three Juniors, envoy-chancellors, participating officials, Viewing Literature grand academicians, and military commissioners—Ball pattern, wearing fish tally;
translations.idiomatic: Gold belts: the three dukes, left and right chancellors, three juniors, envoy-chancellors, participating officials, Viewing Literature grand academicians, and commissioners wore Ball pattern with fish tally;

sentences.zh: 觀文殿學士至華文閣直學士、御史大夫、中丞、六曹尚書、侍郎、散騎常侍、開封尹、給事中並禦仙花，內御史大夫、六曹尚書、觀文殿學士至翰林學士仍佩魚；

translations.literal: Viewing Literature academicians down to Splendid Culture expositor-rank, Censor-in-Chief, Vice Censor-in-Chief, Six Ministries directors, vice ministers, Regular Attendant, Kaifeng Intendant, and Drafting Attendant all wore Immortal Flower; among them Censor-in-Chief, Six Ministries directors, and Viewing Literature academicians down to Hanlin academicians still wore fish tally;
translations.idiomatic: Viewing Literature academicians through Splendid Culture expositor-rank, censors, ministry directors and vice ministers, regular attendants, Kaifeng intendant, and drafting attendants wore Immortal Flower; censors-in-chief, ministry directors, and Viewing Literature academicians through Hanlin still wore fish tally;

sentences.zh: 中書舍人、左右諫議大夫、龍圖天章寶文顯謨徽猷敷文煥章華文閣待制、權侍郎服紅鞓排方黑犀帶，仍佩魚；

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafters, Left and Right Remonstrance Grandees, Dragon Diagram, Heavenly Chapter, Treasuring Literature, Displaying Counsel, Fine Strategy, Spreading Literature, Resplendent Insignia, and Splendid Culture hall academicians-in-waiting, and acting vice ministers wore red-strapped square black rhinoceros belts and still wore fish tally;
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat drafters, remonstrance grandees, hall academicians-in-waiting of the various imperial libraries, and acting vice ministers wore red-strapped square black rhinoceros belts with fish tally;

sentences.zh: 權侍郎以上罷任不帶職者，亦許服之。

translations.literal: Acting vice ministers and above who left office without retaining titles were also permitted to wear them.
translations.idiomatic: Former acting vice ministers and higher ranks without retained titles could still wear them.

sentences.zh: 魚袋。

translations.literal: Fish tally pouch.
translations.idiomatic: The Fish Tally Pouch.

sentences.zh: 其制自唐始，蓋以為符契也。

translations.literal: Its system began in Tang, essentially serving as a tally token.
translations.idiomatic: The practice began in Tang as a tally token.

sentences.zh: 其始曰魚符，左一，右一。

translations.literal: At first it was called fish tally: one left, one right.
translations.idiomatic: Originally called fish tally, there was one left piece and one right piece.

sentences.zh: 左者進內，左者隨身，刻官姓名，出入合之。

translations.literal: The left was presented within; the right was carried on the person—official name engraved; entering and leaving, they were matched.
translations.idiomatic: The left piece was kept in the palace, the right carried on the person, engraved with the official's name and matched on entry and exit.

sentences.zh: 因盛以袋，故曰魚袋。

translations.literal: Because it was stored in a pouch, it was called fish tally pouch.
translations.idiomatic: Because it was kept in a pouch, it was called the fish tally pouch.

sentences.zh: 宋因之，其制以金銀飾為魚形，公服則係於帶而垂於後，以明貴賤，非復如唐之符契也。

translations.literal: Song followed this; its system used gold and silver ornament in fish shape; on official dress it was fastened to the belt and hung behind, to mark noble and base—it was no longer like Tang's tally token.
translations.idiomatic: Song followed the practice with gold or silver fish ornaments fastened to the belt and hanging behind to mark rank, no longer serving as Tang-style tally tokens.

sentences.zh: 太宗雍熙元年，南郊後，內出以賜近臣，由是內外升朝文武官皆佩魚。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxi under Emperor Taizong, after the southern suburban sacrifice, items were issued from within to bestow on intimate ministers; from this, civil and military court officials inside and outside all wore fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizong's Yongxi 1 (984), after the southern suburban sacrifice, fish tally were issued to intimate ministers, and thereafter all court officials wore them.

sentences.zh: 凡服紫者，飾以金；

translations.literal: All who wore purple were ornamented with gold;
translations.idiomatic: Those in purple wore gold fish;

sentences.zh: 服緋者，飾以銀。

translations.literal: those who wore scarlet, with silver.
translations.idiomatic: those in scarlet, silver.

sentences.zh: 庭賜紫，則給金塗銀者；

translations.literal: purple bestowed at court gave gilt silver;
translations.idiomatic: Purple granted at court received gilt silver fish;

sentences.zh: 賜緋，亦有特給者。

translations.literal: scarlet bestowed also had special grants.
translations.idiomatic: scarlet grants sometimes received special fish as well.

sentences.zh: 京官、幕職州縣官賜緋紫者，亦佩。

translations.literal: Capital officials, staff appointees, and prefectural and county officials bestowed scarlet or purple also wore them.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials, staff appointees, and local officials granted scarlet or purple also wore fish tally.

sentences.zh: 親王武官、內職將校皆不佩。

translations.literal: Imperial princes, military officials, and inner staff commanders did not wear them.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes, military officers, and inner-service commanders did not wear them.

sentences.zh: 真宗大中祥符六年，詔伎術官未升朝賜緋、紫者，不得佩魚。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dazhong Xiangfu under Emperor Zhenzong, an edict ordered that technical officers not yet court officials who were bestowed scarlet or purple might not wear fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenzong's Dazhong Xiangfu 6 (1013), technical officers granted scarlet or purple before reaching court rank could not wear fish tally.

sentences.zh: 仁宗天聖二年，翰林待詔、太子中舍同正王文度因勒碑賜紫章服，以舊佩銀魚，請佩金魚。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiansheng under Emperor Renzong, Hanlin Awaiting Edict and Concurrent Regular Palace Steward Wang Wendu, for carving a stele bestowed purple court regalia, because he formerly wore silver fish, requested to wear gold fish.
translations.idiomatic: In Renzong's Tiansheng 2 (1024), Hanlin awaiting-edict Wang Wendu, granted purple regalia for carving a stele, asked to exchange his silver fish for gold.

sentences.zh: 仁宗曰：「先朝不許伎術人輒佩魚，以別士類，不令混淆，宜卻其請。」

translations.literal: Renzong said: "The previous court did not permit technical personnel to wear fish tally at will, to distinguish the scholar class and not allow confusion. His request should be refused."
translations.idiomatic: Renzong said: "The previous court forbade technical officers to wear fish tally, to keep them distinct from scholars. Refuse his request."

sentences.zh: 景祐三年，詔殿中省尚藥奉御賜紫徐安仁，特許佩魚。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingyou, an edict specially permitted Xu Anren, Imperial Pharmacy Attendant of the Palace Directorate bestowed purple, to wear fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyou 3 (1036), Xu Anren of the Imperial Pharmacy, granted purple, was specially allowed to wear fish tally.

sentences.zh: 至和元年，詔：中書提點五房公事，自今雖無出身，亦聽佩魚。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhihe, an edict ordered: Secretariat supervisors of the Five Chambers' business, from now on even without examination pedigree, were also permitted to wear fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhihe 1 (1054), Secretariat supervisors of the Five Chambers could wear fish tally even without examination degrees.

sentences.zh: 舊制，自選人入為堂後官，轉至五房提點，始得佩魚。

translations.literal: Under the old system, from entering as a selection candidate to becoming a rear-hall official, advancing to Five Chambers supervisor, one first obtained fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, one entered as a selection candidate, became a rear-hall clerk, and only as Five Chambers supervisor received fish tally.

sentences.zh: 提點五房呂惟和非選人入，援司天監五官正例求佩魚，特許之。

translations.literal: Five Chambers supervisor Lv Weiyu, not entering by selection candidate route, cited the Astronomical Observatory Five Offices Director precedent to request fish tally and was specially permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Five Chambers supervisor Lv Weiyu, not a selection-route appointee, cited the Astronomical Observatory precedent and was specially granted fish tally.

sentences.zh: 神宗元豐二年，蒲宗孟除翰林學士，神宗曰：「學士職清地近，非它官比，而官儀未寵，自今宜加佩魚。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfeng under Emperor Shenzong, Pu Zongmeng was appointed Hanlin Academician; Shenzong said: "The academician's office is pure and near, not comparable to other offices, yet court ritual has not honored it. From now on fish tally should be added."
translations.idiomatic: In Shenzong's the second year of Yuanfeng (1079), when Pu Zongmeng became Hanlin academician, Shenzong said: "The Hanlin post is eminent and close to the throne, yet its ritual honors are insufficient. Henceforth Hanlin academicians shall wear fish tally."

sentences.zh: 遂著為令。

translations.literal: This was then established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: This became regulation.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔：自今中書堂後官，並帶賜緋魚袋，餘依舊例。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict ordered: from now on Secretariat rear-hall officials all carried bestowed scarlet fish tally pouches; the rest followed old precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, Secretariat rear-hall officials were all granted scarlet fish tally pouches; others followed precedent.

sentences.zh: 徽宗政和元年，尚書兵部侍郎王詔奏：「今監司、守、倅等，並許借服色而不許佩魚，即是有服而無章，殆與吏無別。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenghe under Emperor Huizong, Vice Minister of War Wang Zhao memorialized: "Today supervisory commissioners, prefects, deputies, and the like are all permitted to borrow dress colors but not permitted to wear fish tally—thus having dress but no insignia, scarcely different from clerks.
translations.idiomatic: In Huizong's Zhenghe 1 (1111), Vice Minister of War Wang Zhao argued: "Supervisory commissioners, prefects, and deputies may borrow robe colors but not fish tally—dress without insignia, barely distinct from clerks.

sentences.zh: 乞今後應借緋、紫臣僚，並許隨服色佩魚，仍各許入銜，候回日依舊服色。」

translations.literal: I beg that henceforth all officials borrowing scarlet or purple be permitted to wear fish tally according to dress color, each also permitted to enter it in their title, and on return day resume their original dress colors."
translations.idiomatic: Let all who borrow scarlet or purple also wear matching fish tally and note it in their titles, resuming normal dress on return."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 中興，並仍舊制。

translations.literal: At the Restoration, all still followed the old system.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration, the old rules remained in force.

sentences.zh: 笏。

translations.literal: Court tablet.
translations.idiomatic: The Court Tablet.

sentences.zh: 唐制五品以上用象。

translations.literal: Tang regulations: fifth rank and above used ivory.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang rules, fifth rank and above used ivory tablets.

sentences.zh: 上圓下方；

translations.literal: round above, square below;
translations.idiomatic: Round at the top, square at the bottom;

sentences.zh: 六品以下用竹、木，上挫下方。

translations.literal: sixth rank and below used bamboo or wood, beveled above and square below.
translations.idiomatic: sixth rank and below used bamboo or wood, beveled at the top and square below.

sentences.zh: 宋文散五品以上用象，九品以上用木。

translations.literal: Song civil officials fifth rank and above used ivory; ninth rank and above used wood.
translations.idiomatic: Song civil officials of fifth rank and above used ivory; ninth rank and above used wood.

sentences.zh: 武臣、內職並用象，千牛衣綠亦用象，廷賜緋、綠者給之。

translations.literal: Military officials and inner staff all used ivory; Thousand-Ox guards in green also used ivory; those bestowed scarlet or green at court were given them.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers and inner staff all used ivory; Thousand-Ox guards in green did as well; scarlet or green grants at court included tablets.

sentences.zh: 中興同。

translations.literal: At the Restoration, the same.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration, the same rules applied.

sentences.zh: 靴。

translations.literal: Boots.
translations.idiomatic: Boots.

sentences.zh: 宋初沿舊制，朝履用靴。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song the old system was followed; court footwear used boots.
translations.idiomatic: Early Song followed precedent: court dress used boots.

sentences.zh: 政和更定禮制，改靴用履。

translations.literal: Zhenghe revised ritual regulations, changing boots to shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenghe ritual reform, boots were replaced with court shoes.

sentences.zh: 中興仍之。

translations.literal: At the Restoration this continued.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration, shoes remained in use.

sentences.zh: 乾道七年，復改用靴，以黑革為之，大抵參用履製，惟加靿焉。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qiandao, boots were again adopted, made of black leather, largely following shoe regulations but with added uppers.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao 7 (1171), boots returned, black leather, largely following shoe rules but with higher uppers.

sentences.zh: 其飾亦有絇、繶、純、綦，大夫以上具四飾，朝請、武功郎以下去繶，從義、宣教郎以下至將校、伎術官並去純。

translations.literal: Their ornaments also had laces, side ornaments, borders, and ties; grandees and above had all four ornaments; Court Gentleman and Martial Achievement Gentleman and below removed side ornaments; Following Righteousness and Promoting Instruction Gentlemen and below down to commanders and technical officers all removed borders.
translations.idiomatic: Ornaments included laces, side pieces, borders, and ties; grandees kept all four; Court Gentlemen and below dropped side pieces; lower ranks and technical officers dropped borders as well.

sentences.zh: 底用麻再重，革一重。

translations.literal: Soles used hemp doubled, leather once.
translations.idiomatic: Soles had double hemp layers and one leather layer.

sentences.zh: 裏用素衲氈，高八寸。

translations.literal: Linings used plain quilted felt, eight inches high.
translations.idiomatic: Linings were plain quilted felt, eight inches high.

sentences.zh: 諸文武官通服之，惟以四飾為別。

translations.literal: All civil and military officials wore them in common, distinguished only by the four ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: All civil and military officials wore them, distinguished only by the four ornaments.

sentences.zh: 服綠者飾以綠，服緋、紫者飾亦如之，仿古隨裳色之意。

translations.literal: Wearers of green were ornamented with green; wearers of scarlet and purple likewise—imitating antiquity's meaning of following garment color.
translations.idiomatic: Green robes had green ornaments; scarlet and purple likewise, reviving the ancient practice of matching footwear to dress.

sentences.zh: 簪戴。

translations.literal: Flower wearing.
translations.idiomatic: Flower Wearing.

sentences.zh: 襆頭簪花，謂之簪戴。

translations.literal: Flowers pinned in the futou headwrap were called flower wearing.
translations.idiomatic: Flowers pinned in the futou were called "flower wearing."

sentences.zh: 中興，郊祀、明堂禮畢回鑾，臣僚及扈從並簪花，恭謝日亦如之。

translations.literal: At the Restoration, after suburban sacrifice and Bright Hall rites when the imperial carriage returned, officials and escorts all wore flowers; on thanksgiving days it was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration, officials and escorts wore flowers when the emperor returned from suburban and Bright Hall rites, and on thanksgiving days as well.

sentences.zh: 大羅花以紅、黃、銀紅三色，欒枝以雜色羅，大絹花以紅、銀紅二色。

translations.literal: Large gauze flowers used red, yellow, and silver-red three colors; spray branches used mixed-color gauze; large silk flowers used red and silver-red two colors.
translations.idiomatic: Large gauze flowers came in red, yellow, and silver-red; spray branches in mixed gauze; large silk flowers in red and silver-red.

sentences.zh: 羅花以賜百官，欒枝，卿監以上有之；

translations.literal: Gauze flowers were bestowed on the hundred officials; spray branches, directors and supervisors and above had them;
translations.idiomatic: Gauze flowers went to all officials; spray branches to directors and above;

sentences.zh: 絹花以賜將校以下。

translations.literal: silk flowers were bestowed on commanders and below.
translations.idiomatic: silk flowers to commanders and below.

sentences.zh: 太上兩宮上壽畢，及聖節、及錫宴、及賜新進士聞喜宴，並如之。

translations.literal: After longevity celebrations for the two palaces of the retired emperor, and on imperial birthdays, grant banquets, and new jinshi celebratory banquets, all were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The same applied after the retired emperor's longevity celebrations, on imperial birthdays, at grant banquets, and at new jinshi celebratory feasts.

sentences.zh: 重戴。

translations.literal: Chongdai hat.
translations.idiomatic: The Chongdai Hat.

sentences.zh: 唐士人多尚之，蓋古大裁帽之遺製，本野夫岩叟之服。

translations.literal: Tang scholars mostly favored it; it was essentially the surviving form of the ancient large-cut cap, originally the dress of wild men and cliff elders.
translations.idiomatic: Tang scholars favored it—a survival of the ancient large-cut cap, originally worn by recluses and mountain elders.

sentences.zh: 以皂羅為之，方而垂簷，紫裏，兩紫絲組為纓，垂而結之頷下。

translations.literal: It was made of black gauze, square with hanging brim, purple lining, two purple silk cords as tassel hanging and knotted below the chin.
translations.idiomatic: It was black gauze, square with a hanging brim, purple lined, with two purple silk cords knotted under the chin.

sentences.zh: 所謂重戴者，蓋折上巾又加以帽焉。

translations.literal: What is called chongdai is essentially the folded-up cap with a hat placed atop it.
translations.idiomatic: The so-called chongdai was the folded-up cap with a hat worn over it.

sentences.zh: 宋初，御史臺皆重戴，餘官或戴或否。

translations.literal: In early Song, everyone in the Censorate wore chongdai; other officials wore it or not.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song, the entire Censorate wore the chongdai; other officials might or might not.

sentences.zh: 後新進士亦戴，至釋褐則止。

translations.literal: Later new jinshi also wore it; upon leaving coarse dress for office they ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Later, new jinshi wore it too, until they left student dress upon taking office.

sentences.zh: 太宗淳化二年，御史臺言：「舊儀，三院御史在台及出使，並重戴，事已久廢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua under Taizong, the Censorate said: "By old ritual, censors of the three bureaus at the bureau and on mission all wore chongdai; the practice has long been abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In 991, the Censorate reported: "Under the old ritual, censors of all three bureaus at headquarters and on assignment wore the chongdai—a custom long abandoned.

sentences.zh: 其御史出台為省職及在京厘務者，請依舊儀，違者罰俸一月。」

translations.literal: Censors who leave the bureau for provincial posts and those handling duties in the capital—request following the old ritual; violators fined one month's salary."
translations.idiomatic: For censors posted to provincial offices or handling business in the capital, we ask that the old ritual be restored; violators shall forfeit one month's salary."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 又詔兩省及尚書省五品以上皆重戴，樞密三司使、副則不。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered both Secretariats and Secretariat officials of the fifth rank and above all to wear chongdai; Bureau of Military Affairs and Fiscal Commission commissioners and deputies did not.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also required fifth-rank officials and above in both Secretariats and the Secretariat to wear the chongdai; Military Affairs and Fiscal Commission chiefs and deputies did not.

sentences.zh: 中興後，御史、兩製、知貢舉官、新進士上三人，許服之。

translations.literal: After the restoration, censors, drafters of both academies, examination commissioners, and the top three new jinshi were permitted to wear it.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration, censors, Hanlin drafters, chief examiners, and the top three new jinshi were allowed to wear it.

sentences.zh: 時服。

translations.literal: Seasonal dress.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal Dress Gifts

sentences.zh: 宋初因五代舊制，每歲諸臣皆賜時服，然止賜將相、學士、禁軍大校。

translations.literal: Early Song followed the Five Dynasties old system: each year all ministers were given seasonal dress, yet only generals and chancellors, academicians, and senior palace-guard officers received it.
translations.idiomatic: Early Song followed the Five Dynasties practice of annual seasonal gifts, but only chief ministers, academicians, and senior palace-guard officers received them.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，太祖謂侍臣曰：「百官不賜，甚無謂也。」

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong, Taizu said to attending ministers: "Not giving to the hundred officials is quite meaningless."
translations.idiomatic: In 962, Taizu told his attendants: "Leaving the whole bureaucracy out makes no sense at all.

sentences.zh: 乃遍賜之。

translations.literal: Then he gave to all universally.
translations.idiomatic: He then extended the gift to everyone.

sentences.zh: 歲遇端午、十月一日，文武群臣將校皆給焉。

translations.literal: Each year at the Dragon Boat Festival and the first day of the tenth month, all civil and military ministers and officers were given them.
translations.idiomatic: Every year at the Dragon Boat Festival and on the first day of the tenth month, civil and military officials and officers all received seasonal dress.

sentences.zh: 是歲十月，近臣、軍校增給錦襯袍，中書門下、樞密、宣徽院、節度使及侍衛步軍都虞候以上，皇親大將軍以上，天下樂暈錦；

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month, close ministers and military officers were additionally given lined brocade robes: Secretariat-Chancellery, Military Affairs, Palace Service, military commissioners, and Palace Guard infantry chief commandants and above, and imperial clansmen major generals and above, received All-Under-Heaven-Rejoicing halo brocade;
translations.idiomatic: That October, close ministers and officers also received lined brocade robes. Secretariat-Chancellery, Military Affairs, Palace Service, military commissioners, Palace Guard infantry chief commandants and above, and imperial clansmen major generals and above received All-Under-Heaven-Rejoicing halo brocade;

sentences.zh: 三司使、學士、中丞、內客省使、駙馬、留後、觀察使，皇親將軍、諸司使、廂主以上，簇四盤雕細錦；

translations.literal: Fiscal commissioners, academicians, vice censors, Inner Store commissioners, consorts-in-law, regents, and observation commissioners; imperial clansmen generals, various commissioners, and commandery chiefs and above, received Cluster-Four-Trays carved fine brocade;
translations.idiomatic: Fiscal commissioners, academicians, vice censors, Inner Store commissioners, consorts, regents, and observation commissioners; imperial clansmen generals, bureau commissioners, and commandery chiefs and above received Cluster-Four-Trays carved fine brocade;

sentences.zh: 三司副使、宮觀判官，黃師子大錦；

translations.literal: Fiscal deputy commissioners and palace-abbey judges received yellow lion-cub great brocade;
translations.idiomatic: Fiscal deputies and palace-abbey judges received Yellow Lion Cub great brocade;

sentences.zh: 防禦團練使、刺史、皇親諸司副使，翠毛細錦；

translations.literal: Defense-train commissioners, prefects, and imperial-clan various deputy commissioners received emerald-feather fine brocade;
translations.idiomatic: Defense-train commissioners, prefects, and imperial-clan deputy commissioners received emerald-feather fine brocade;

sentences.zh: 權中丞、知開封府、銀台司、審刑院及待制以上，知檢院鼓院、同三司副使、六統軍、金吾大將軍，紅錦。

translations.literal: Acting vice censors, Kaifeng prefect, Silver Platform Office, Review Court, and drafters and above; inspection and drum-court officials; those equal to fiscal deputies; six army commanders; and Golden Guard major generals received red brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Acting vice censors, the Kaifeng prefect, Silver Platform and Review Court officials, drafters and above, inspection and drum-court officers, fiscal-deputy equivalents, six army commanders, and Golden Guard major generals received red brocade.

sentences.zh: 諸班及諸軍將校，亦賜窄錦袍。

translations.literal: Various guard ranks and army officers also received narrow brocade robes.
translations.idiomatic: Guard officers and army commanders also received narrow brocade robes.

sentences.zh: 有翠毛、宜男、雲雁細錦，師子、練鵲、寶照大錦，寶照中錦，凡七等。

translations.literal: There were emerald-feather, Propitious Male, and Cloud-Goose fine brocades; lion, trained magpie, and Treasure-Shine great brocades; and Treasure-Shine medium brocade—seven grades in all.
translations.idiomatic: Patterns included emerald-feather, Propitious Male, and Cloud-Goose fine brocades; lion, trained magpie, and Treasure-Shine great brocades; and Treasure-Shine medium brocade—seven grades in all.

sentences.zh: 應給錦袍者，皆五事；

translations.literal: Those due brocade robes all received five items;
translations.idiomatic: Recipients of brocade robes received five items each;

sentences.zh: 〈（公服、錦寬袍，綾汗衫、袴，勒帛，丞郎、給舍、大卿監以上不給錦袍者，加以黃綾繡抱肚。）〉

translations.literal: (official dress, brocade wide robe, gauze undershirt and trousers, and girdle belt; for vice directors, drafting compilers, and grand supervisors and above not given brocade robes, a yellow gauze embroidered belly band was added.)
translations.idiomatic: (official dress, brocade wide robe, gauze undershirt and trousers, and girdle belt; vice directors, drafting compilers, and grand supervisors and above who did not receive brocade robes also received a yellow gauze embroidered belly band.)

sentences.zh: 大將軍、少卿監、郎中以上，樞密諸房副承旨以上，諸司使，皇親承製、崇班，皆四事；

translations.literal: Major generals, vice supervisors and directors, bureau directors and above, Military Affairs deputy commissioners and above, various commissioners, and imperial-clan appointees and honored ranks all received four items;
translations.idiomatic: Major generals, vice directors and supervisors, bureau directors and above, Military Affairs deputy commissioners and above, bureau commissioners, and imperial-clan appointees and honored ranks received four items each;

translations.literal: (no brocade robe.)
translations.idiomatic: (no brocade robe.)

sentences.zh: 將軍至副率、知雜御史至大理正、入內都知、內侍都知、皇親殿直以上，皆三事；

translations.literal: Generals through deputy commandants; assorted censors through Court of Judicial Review directors; Inner Service directors; eunuch directors; and imperial-clan palace appointees and above all received three items;
translations.idiomatic: Generals through deputy commandants, assorted censors through Review Court directors, Inner Service directors, eunuch directors, and imperial-clan palace appointees and above received three items each;

translations.literal: (no trousers.)
translations.idiomatic: (no trousers.)

sentences.zh: 通事舍人、承製、崇班、入內押班、內侍副都知押班、內常侍、六尚奉御以下，京官充館閣、宗正寺、刑法官者，皆二事；

translations.literal: Herald registrars, appointees, honored ranks, Inner Service deputy directors, eunuch deputy directors, inner regular attendants, six inner offices attendants and below, and capital officials serving in institutes, the clanship court, or judicial offices all received two items;
translations.idiomatic: Herald registrars, appointees, honored ranks, Inner Service and eunuch deputy directors, inner regular attendants, six inner-office attendants and below, and capital officials in institutes, the clanship court, or judicial offices received two items each;

sentences.zh: 〈（無勒帛，內職汗衫以綾，文臣以絹。）〉

translations.literal: (no girdle belt; inner staff undershirts were of gauze, civil officials' of silk.)
translations.idiomatic: (no girdle belt; inner staff received gauze undershirts, civil officials silk ones.)

sentences.zh: 閣門祗候、內供奉官至殿直，京官編修、校勘，止給公服。

translations.literal: Gate attendants, inner tribute officials through palace appointees, and capital officials compiling or collating received only official dress.
translations.idiomatic: Gate attendants, inner tribute officials through palace appointees, and capital officials who compiled or collated received only official dress.

sentences.zh: 端午，亦給。

translations.literal: At the Dragon Boat Festival, gifts were also given.
translations.idiomatic: The Dragon Boat Festival brought gifts as well.

sentences.zh: 應給錦袍者，汗衫以黃縠，別加繡抱肚、小扇。

translations.literal: Those due brocade robes received undershirts of yellow gauze weave, with an embroidered belly band and small fan added.
translations.idiomatic: Brocade-robe recipients also received yellow gauze-weave undershirts, plus an embroidered belly band and a small fan.

sentences.zh: 誕聖節所給，如時服。

translations.literal: Gifts on the Sage's Birthday festival matched the seasonal dress.
translations.idiomatic: Birthday-of-the-Sage gifts followed the same rules as seasonal dress.

sentences.zh: 〈（京師禁廂軍校、衛士、內諸司胥史、工巧人，並給服有差。）〉

translations.literal: (Capital forbidden guards officers and guards, inner various offices clerks, and artisans all received dress in differing grades.)
translations.idiomatic: (Capital forbidden-guard officers and guards, inner-office clerks, and artisans all received graded clothing.)

sentences.zh: 朝官、京官、內職出為外任通判、監押、巡檢以上者，

translations.literal: Court officials, capital officials, and inner staff posted outside as superintendents, supervisors, or inspectors and above,
translations.idiomatic: Court officials, capital officials, and inner staff posted outside as superintendents, supervisors, or inspectors and above,

sentences.zh: 〈（大藩府監務者，亦或給之。）〉

translations.literal: (commissioners of great prefectures sometimes also received gifts.)
translations.idiomatic: (commissioners of major prefectures sometimes received them as well.)

sentences.zh: 每歲十月時服，開寶中，皆賜窄錦袍。

translations.literal: Each year for tenth-month seasonal dress, in the Kaibao period all were given narrow brocade robes.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao era, everyone posted outside received narrow brocade robes each year for the tenth-month seasonal gift.

sentences.zh: 太平興國以後，文官知制誥、武官上將軍、內職諸司使以上，皆賜錦。

translations.literal: After Taiping-Xingguo, civil officials who drafted edicts, military officials of senior general rank, and inner various commissioners and above all received brocade.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiping-Xingguo, edict drafters, senior generals, and inner bureau commissioners and above all received brocade.

sentences.zh: 〈（藩鎮觀察使以上，天下樂暈錦；

translations.literal: (Frontier observation commissioners and above received All-Under-Heaven-Rejoicing halo brocade;
translations.idiomatic: (Observation commissioners and above received All-Under-Heaven-Rejoicing halo brocade;

sentences.zh: 尚書及步軍都虞候以上及知益州、并州，次暈錦，皆五事。

translations.literal: Secretariat directors, infantry chief commandants and above, and prefects of Yizhou and Bingzhou received secondary halo brocade—all five items.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat directors, infantry chief commandants and above, and the prefects of Yizhou and Bingzhou received secondary halo brocade—five items each.

sentences.zh: 學士、丞郎，簇四盤雕錦；

translations.literal: Academicians and vice directors received Cluster-Four-Trays carved brocade;
translations.idiomatic: Academicians and vice directors received Cluster-Four-Trays carved brocade;

sentences.zh: 刺史以上及知廣州，翠毛錦，皆三件。

translations.literal: Prefects and above and the prefect of Guangzhou received emerald-feather brocade—three items each.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and above and the Guangzhou prefect received emerald-feather brocade—three items each.

sentences.zh: 待制以上、橫班諸司使，翠毛錦；

translations.literal: Drafters and above and lateral-rank various commissioners received emerald-feather brocade;
translations.idiomatic: Drafters and above and lateral-rank bureau commissioners received emerald-feather brocade;

sentences.zh: 知代州，禦仙花錦；

translations.literal: The prefect of Daizhou received Imperial-Immortal-Flower brocade;
translations.idiomatic: The Daizhou prefect received Imperial-Immortal-Flower brocade;

sentences.zh: 諸司使領郡，宜男錦；

translations.literal: Various commissioners holding prefectures received Propitious Male brocade;
translations.idiomatic: Bureau commissioners who also held prefectures received Propitious Male brocade;

sentences.zh: 諸司使，雲雁錦。

translations.literal: Various commissioners received Cloud-Goose brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau commissioners received Cloud-Goose brocade.

sentences.zh: 駙馬，錦如丞郎，增至四事。

translations.literal: Consorts-in-law received brocade like vice directors, increased to four items.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts received brocade like vice directors, raised to four items.

sentences.zh: 益州鈐轄，錦從本官，增綾袴。）〉

translations.literal: The Yizhou military commander followed his base rank for brocade and received an additional pair of gauze trousers.)
translations.idiomatic: The Yizhou military commander followed his base rank for brocade and also received gauze trousers.)

sentences.zh: 朝官供奉官以上，皆賜紫地皂花欹正。

translations.literal: Court officials of tribute-official rank and above all received purple-ground black-flower slanting-front robes.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials of tribute-official rank and above received purple-ground black-flower slanting-front robes.

sentences.zh: 京官殿直以下，皆賜紫大綾。

translations.literal: Capital officials of palace-appointee rank and below all received great purple gauze.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials at palace-appointee rank and below received great purple gauze.

sentences.zh: 在外禁軍將校，亦賜窄錦袍，次賜紫綾色絹。

translations.literal: Forbidden-army officers posted outside also received narrow brocade robes, and secondarily purple gauze-colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: Posted forbidden-army officers also received narrow brocade robes, then purple gauze-colored silk.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，始詔河北、河東、陝西三路轉運使、副，並給方勝練鵲錦。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde, an edict first ordered transport commissioners and deputies of the Hebei, Hedong, and Shaanxi three circuits all to receive Square-Victory trained-magpie brocade.
translations.idiomatic: In 1004, transport commissioners and deputies on the Hebei, Hedong, and Shaanxi circuits were first ordered to receive Square-Victory trained-magpie brocade.

sentences.zh: 校獵從官兼賜紫羅錦、旋襴、暖靴。

translations.literal: Retinue officials at the hunt additionally received purple gauze brocade, twisted damask, and warm boots.
translations.idiomatic: Hunting retinue officials also received purple gauze brocade, twisted damask, and warm boots.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年，令節度使給皂地金線盤雲鳳鹿胎旋襴，侍衛步軍都虞候以上給皂地金線盤花鴛鴦。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongxi, military commissioners were ordered to receive black-ground gold-thread coiled cloud-phoenix-deer-fetus twisted damask; Palace Guard infantry chief commandants and above received black-ground gold-thread coiled-flower mandarin ducks.
translations.idiomatic: In 987, military commissioners received black-ground gold-thread coiled cloud-phoenix-deer-fetus twisted damask; Palace Guard infantry chief commandants and above received black-ground gold-thread coiled-flower mandarin ducks.

sentences.zh: 親王、宰相、使相生日，並賜衣五事，錦彩百匹，金花銀器百兩，馬二匹，金塗銀鞍勒一。

translations.literal: On the birthdays of princes, chancellors, and commissioner-prime ministers, each was given five garments, a hundred bolts of brocade silk, a hundred taels of gold-flower silver vessels, two horses, and one gold-plated silver saddle and bridle.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, chancellors, and commissioner-prime ministers each received five garments, a hundred bolts of brocade silk, a hundred taels of gold-flower silver vessels, two horses, and a gold-plated silver saddle and bridle on their birthdays.

sentences.zh: 宰相、樞密使、參知政事、樞密副使、宣徽使初拜、加恩中謝日，並賜衣五事，金帶一，

translations.literal: On the first appointment and grace mid-thanks days of the chancellor, Military Affairs commissioner, Vice Grand Councilor, Military Affairs deputy, and Palace Service commissioner, each was given five garments and one gold belt,
translations.idiomatic: On first appointment and grace mid-thanks days, the chancellor, Military Affairs commissioner, Vice Grand Councilor, Military Affairs deputy, and Palace Service commissioner each received five garments and a gold belt,

sentences.zh: 〈（舊荔支帶，淳化後，宰相、參知政事、文臣任樞密副使，改賜方團胯球路金帶，加以金魚。）〉

translations.literal: (Formerly the Lychee belt; after Chunhua, the chancellor, Vice Grand Councilor, and civil officials serving as Military Affairs deputy were changed to square-round hip Ball-Road gold belts with gold fish tallies added.)
translations.idiomatic: (They had formerly received the Lychee belt; after Chunhua, the chancellor, Vice Grand Councilor, and civil Military Affairs deputies received square-round hip Ball-Road gold belts with gold fish tallies.)

sentences.zh: 塗金銀鞍勒馬一。

translations.literal: and one horse with gold-plated silver saddle and bridle.
translations.idiomatic: And one horse with a gold-plated silver saddle and bridle.

sentences.zh: 三司使、學士、御史中丞初拜中謝日，賜衣五事，荔支金帶一，塗金銀鞍勒馬一。

translations.literal: On the first appointment mid-thanks day of the fiscal commissioner, academicians, and censor vice-director, each was given five garments, one Lychee gold belt, and one gold-plated silver saddle-and-bridle horse.
translations.idiomatic: On first appointment mid-thanks days, fiscal commissioners, academicians, and censor vice-directors received five garments, a Lychee gold belt, and a horse with gold-plated silver saddle and bridle.

sentences.zh: 〈（文明學士以下，初賜金裝犀帶，後改賜金帶。）〉

translations.literal: (Civilized Court academicians and below were initially given gold-mounted rhinoceros belts; later they were changed to gold belts.)
translations.idiomatic: (Civilized Court academicians and below first received gold-mounted rhinoceros belts, later changed to gold belts.)

sentences.zh: 中書舍人，賜襲衣、犀帶。

translations.literal: Secretariat drafting officials were given court dress and rhinoceros belts.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat drafting officials received court dress and rhinoceros belts.

sentences.zh: 宰相以下對禦抬賜；

translations.literal: The chancellor and below received gifts in person before the throne;
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor and those below him received gifts in person before the throne;

sentences.zh: 樞密直學士、中書舍人謝訖，中使押賜，再入謝於別殿。

translations.literal: after thanks, Military Affairs direct academicians and Secretariat drafting officials had an inner envoy escort the gift, then entered again to give thanks in a separate hall.
translations.idiomatic: Military Affairs direct academicians and Secretariat drafting officials, after giving thanks, received gifts from an inner envoy and thanked again in a side hall.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人或告謝日已改賜章服，則罷中使押賜。

translations.literal: If a Secretariat drafting official on the thanks day had already been changed to bestowed insignia dress, the inner envoy escort was discontinued.
