translations.idiomatic: If a drafting official had already received insignia dress on the thanks day, the inner envoy escort was omitted.

sentences.zh: 郊禋禮畢，親王、宰相至龍圖閣直學士、禁軍將校，各賜襲衣、金帶，

translations.literal: After the suburban ceremony, princes, chancellors through Dragon Pavilion direct academicians, and forbidden-army officers each received court dress and gold belts,
translations.idiomatic: After the suburban rites, princes, chancellors through Dragon Pavilion direct academicians, and forbidden-army officers each received court dress and gold belts,

sentences.zh: 〈（親王、中書門下、樞密、宣徽、三司使、四廂都指揮使以上，加鞍勒馬一。

translations.literal: (Princes; Secretariat-Chancellery; Military Affairs; Palace Service; Fiscal Commission; and four wing chief commanders and above received one additional saddle horse.
translations.idiomatic: (Princes; Secretariat-Chancellery; Military Affairs; Palace Service; Fiscal Commission; and four-wing chief commanders and above also received a saddle horse;

sentences.zh: 其後宮觀副使、天書扶侍使，並同學士。）〉

translations.literal: Later, palace-abbey deputy commissioners and Heavenly Book attendant commissioners were treated the same as academicians.)
translations.idiomatic: later, palace-abbey deputy commissioners and Heavenly Book attendant commissioners were treated like academicians.)

sentences.zh: 同中謝日。

translations.literal: The procedure matched the mid-thanks day.
translations.idiomatic: The procedure matched mid-thanks day.

sentences.zh: 雍熙元年，兩省五品以上，御史臺、尚書省四品以上，各賜襲衣、犀帶、魚袋。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxi, fifth-rank officials and above in both Secretariats and fourth-rank officials and above in the Censorate and Secretariat each received court dress, rhinoceros belts, and fish pouches.
translations.idiomatic: In 984, fifth-rank officials and above in both Secretariats and fourth-rank officials and above in the Censorate and Secretariat each received court dress, rhinoceros belts, and fish pouches.

sentences.zh: 其為五使，則皆賜金帶，仍各加器幣。

translations.literal: Those serving as the Five Commissioners all received gold belts and additionally ritual vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Commissioners all received gold belts plus ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 〈（文武行事官，各賜金帛。

translations.literal: (Civil and military procession officials each received gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: (Civil and military procession officials each received gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 牧伯在外者，遇大禮，不賜。

translations.literal: Regional governors posted outside did not receive gifts when great rites occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Regional governors posted outside received nothing on great rites.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，詔節度、觀察、防禦、團練使，刺史，因東封為諸州部署鈐轄者，並特賜焉。）〉

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, an edict ordered military, observation, defense-train commissioners and prefects who served as deployment military commanders for the eastern march all to receive special gifts.)
translations.idiomatic: In 1008, military, observation, and defense-train commissioners and prefects serving as deployment commanders for the eastern march were specially included.)

sentences.zh: 使相、節度使自鎮來朝入見日，賜衣五事，金帶，鞍馬；

translations.literal: On the audience day when commissioner-prime ministers and military commissioners came from their posts to court, each was given five garments, a gold belt, and saddle horses;
translations.idiomatic: When commissioner-prime ministers and military commissioners came from their posts for audience, they received five garments, a gold belt, and saddle horses;

sentences.zh: 朝辭日，賜窄衣六事，金束帶，鞍勒馬一，散馬二；

translations.literal: on the farewell-audience day, each was given six items of narrow dress, a gold binding belt, one saddle horse, and two loose horses;
translations.idiomatic: on the farewell audience they received six items of narrow dress, a gold binding belt, one saddle horse, and two loose horses;

sentences.zh: 〈（節度使減散馬。）〉

translations.literal: (Military commissioners had the loose horses reduced.)
translations.idiomatic: (military commissioners received fewer loose horses.)

sentences.zh: 為都部署者，別賜帶甲鞍勒馬一。

translations.literal: Those serving as overall deployment commanders separately received one armored saddle horse.
translations.idiomatic: Overall deployment commanders also received an armored saddle horse.

sentences.zh: 觀察使為都部署、副都部署赴本任、知州，賜窄衣三事，金束帶，鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: Observation commissioners serving as deployment or deputy deployment commanders, or as prefects going to their posts, received three items of narrow dress, a gold binding belt, and a saddle horse.
translations.idiomatic: Observation commissioners serving as deployment or deputy deployment commanders, or prefects heading to post, received three items of narrow dress, a gold binding belt, and a saddle horse.

sentences.zh: 防禦團練使、刺史為部署、鈐轄，賜窄衣三事，金束帶；

translations.literal: Defense-train commissioners and prefects serving as deployment or military commanders received three items of narrow dress and a gold binding belt;
translations.idiomatic: Defense-train commissioners and prefects serving as deployment or military commanders received three items of narrow dress and a gold binding belt;

sentences.zh: 赴本任，賜窄衣三事，塗金銀腰帶；

translations.literal: on going to their posts they received three items of narrow dress and a gold-plated silver waist belt;
translations.idiomatic: on departure for post they received three items of narrow dress and a gold-plated silver waist belt;

sentences.zh: 為知州、都監，賜窄衣三事，絹三十匹。

translations.literal: as prefect or chief supervisor they received three items of narrow dress and thirty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: as prefect or chief supervisor they received three items of narrow dress and thirty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 諸司為鈐轄者，賜窄衣、金束帶。

translations.literal: Various commissioners serving as military commanders received narrow dress and a gold binding belt.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau commissioners serving as military commanders received narrow dress and a gold binding belt.

sentences.zh: 文武官內職出為知州軍、通判、發運、轉運使副、提點刑獄、都監、巡檢、砦主、軍使及任使繁要者，僕射賜窄衣三事，絹五十匹；

translations.literal: Civil and military officials and inner staff posted outside as prefecture-military superintendents, vice prefects, transport commissioners or deputies, judicial intendants, chief supervisors, inspectors, fort chiefs, army commissioners, or holders of important appointments: Vice Directors received three items of narrow dress and fifty bolts of silk;
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials and inner staff posted as prefecture superintendents, vice prefects, transport commissioners or deputies, judicial intendants, chief supervisors, inspectors, fort chiefs, army commissioners, or to important posts received graded gifts—Vice Directors three items of narrow dress and fifty bolts of silk;

sentences.zh: 尚書、丞郎、學士、諫舍、待制、大卿監及統軍、上將軍、諸司使，減絹二十匹；

translations.literal: Secretariat Directors, vice directors, academicians, remonstrance and drafting officials, drafters, grand supervisors, army commanders, senior generals, and various commissioners had the silk reduced by twenty bolts;
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Directors, vice directors, academicians, remonstrance and drafting officials, drafters, grand supervisors, army commanders, senior generals, and bureau commissioners received twenty bolts less;

sentences.zh: 少卿監至五官正、大將軍至副率、諸司副使，減絹一十匹；

translations.literal: vice supervisors through Five Offices directors, major generals through deputy commandants, and various deputy commissioners had the silk reduced by ten bolts;
translations.idiomatic: vice supervisors through Five Offices directors, major generals through deputy commandants, and deputy commissioners received ten bolts less;

sentences.zh: 中郎將、京官內殿承製至借職、內常侍，減衣二事，又減絹一十匹。

translations.literal: central cadet guards; capital officials from inner-hall appointee through borrowed rank; and inner regular attendants had garments reduced by two items and silk by another ten bolts.
translations.idiomatic: central cadet guards, capital officials from inner-hall appointee through borrowed rank, and inner regular attendants lost two garments and another ten bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 窄衣，起二月給紫羅衫；

translations.literal: For narrow dress, from the second month purple gauze shirts were issued;
translations.idiomatic: Narrow dress began with purple gauze shirts issued from the second month;

sentences.zh: 起十月給紫欹正錦襖。

translations.literal: from the tenth month purple slanting-front brocade jackets were issued.
translations.idiomatic: from the tenth month, purple slanting-front brocade jackets.

sentences.zh: 〈（給公服者，單夾亦然。）〉

translations.literal: (Those issued public dress likewise received single-layer and lined garments.)
translations.idiomatic: (Recipients of public dress received both unlined and lined garments as well.)

sentences.zh: 諸道衙內指揮使、都虞候入貢辭日，賜紫羅窄衫，金塗銀帶。

translations.literal: On days when circuit palace-guard commandants and chief adjutants presented tribute and took leave of audience, they were given purple gauze narrow shirts and gold-plated silver belts.
translations.idiomatic: When circuit palace-guard commandants and chief adjutants came to present tribute or bid farewell at court, they received purple gauze narrow shirts and gold-plated silver belts.

sentences.zh: 士庶人車服之制。

translations.literal: Regulations on carriages and dress for gentry and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations governing carriages and dress among the gentry and common people.

sentences.zh: 太宗太平興國七年，詔曰：「士庶之間，車服之制，至於喪葬，各有等差。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo, Emperor Taizong issued an edict saying: "Between gentry and commoners, regulations for carriages and dress, extending even to funerals, each have their proper grades.
translations.idiomatic: In 982, Emperor Taizong decreed: "Among gentry and commoners alike, rules for carriages, clothing, and even burial each observe their proper ranks.

sentences.zh: 近年以來，頗成逾僭。

translations.literal: In recent years these have come to exceed proper rank considerably.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years, however, people have grown brazen in overstepping those ranks.

sentences.zh: 宣令翰林學士承旨李昉詳定以聞。」

translations.literal: He ordered Academician-Recipient Li Fang of the Hanlin Academy to draft detailed regulations and report."
translations.idiomatic: He directed Li Fang, Academician-Recipient of the Hanlin Academy, to work out detailed rules and report back."

sentences.zh: 昉奏：「今後富商大賈乘馬，漆素鞍者勿禁。

translations.literal: Li Fang memorialized: "Henceforth wealthy merchants riding horses with lacquered plain saddles should not be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fang replied: "Henceforth wealthy merchants who ride horses with plain lacquered saddles should not be barred.

sentences.zh: 近年品官綠袍及舉子白襴下皆服紫色，亦請禁之。

translations.literal: In recent years ranked officials in green robes and examination candidates under white barred robes have all worn purple; please forbid this as well.
translations.idiomatic: Lately ranked officials in green robes and examination candidates beneath white barred robes have all taken to wearing purple; I ask that this be forbidden as well.

sentences.zh: 其私第便服，許紫皂衣、白袍。

translations.literal: For informal dress in private residences, purple-black garments and white robes are permitted.
translations.idiomatic: For informal wear at home, purple-black garments and white robes may still be allowed.

sentences.zh: 舊制，庶人服白，今請流外官及貢舉人、庶人通許服皂。

translations.literal: Under the old rule commoners wore white; now I petition that off-register officials, examination candidates, and commoners universally be permitted to wear black.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom commoners wore white; I now ask that off-register officials, examination candidates, and commoners alike be allowed to wear black.

sentences.zh: 工商、庶人家乘簷子，或用四人、八人，請禁斷，聽乘車；

translations.literal: Merchants, artisans, and commoner households riding sedan chairs borne by four or eight men—petition to forbid this and allow only wheeled carriages;
translations.idiomatic: Merchants, artisans, and common households who ride sedan chairs with four or eight bearers should be stopped from doing so and allowed only wheeled carriages;

sentences.zh: 兜子，舁不得過二人。」

translations.literal: for carrying-couches, no more than two bearers."
translations.idiomatic: and for carrying-couches, no more than two bearers."

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved all of it.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年，詔縣鎮場務諸色公人並庶人、商賈、伎術、不係官伶人，只許服皂、白衣，鐵、角帶，不得服紫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duangong, an edict ordered that county clerks, market agents, all categories of public runners, commoners, merchants, artisans, and unofficial entertainers might wear only black or white garments and iron or horn belts, not purple.
translations.idiomatic: In 989, an edict limited county clerks, market agents, public runners of every sort, commoners, merchants, artisans, and private entertainers to black or white dress and iron or horn belts, forbidding purple.

sentences.zh: 文武升朝官及諸司副使、禁軍指揮使、廂軍都虞候之家子弟，不拘此限。

translations.literal: Sons of civil and military officials who attended court, vice commissioners of various bureaus, commandants of the palace guard, and chief adjutants of local garrisons were not bound by this limit.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of civil and military court officials, bureau vice commissioners, palace-guard commandants, and garrison chief adjutants were exempt.

sentences.zh: 襆頭巾子，自今高不過二寸五分。

translations.literal: Futou crests from now on were to be no more than two cun and five fen in height.
translations.idiomatic: Futou crests were henceforth capped at two cun and five fen in height.

sentences.zh: 婦人假髻並宜禁斷，仍不得作高髻及高冠。

translations.literal: Women's false topknots should be forbidden, and high chignons and tall crowns were also not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Women's false topknots were to be banned outright, along with high chignons and tall crowns.

sentences.zh: 其銷金、泥金、真珠裝綴衣服，除命婦許服外，餘人並禁。

translations.literal: Gold-leaf, gold-paste, and pearl-trimmed garments were forbidden to all except titled ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Garments trimmed with gold leaf, gold paste, or pearls were forbidden to everyone except titled ladies.

sentences.zh: 至道元年，復許庶人服紫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao, commoners were again permitted to wear purple.
translations.idiomatic: In 995, commoners were again allowed to wear purple.

sentences.zh: 真宗咸平四年，禁民間造銀鞍瓦、金線、盤蹙金線。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianping, Emperor Zhenzong forbade private manufacture of silver saddle tiles, gold thread, and coiled gold thread.
translations.idiomatic: In 1001, Emperor Zhenzong banned the private making of silver saddle tiles, gold thread, and coiled gold thread.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，三司言：「竊惟山澤之寶，所得至難，儻縱銷釋，實為虛費。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, the Finance Commission reported: "The treasures of mountains and marshes are hardest to obtain; if melting and consumption were permitted, it would be true waste.
translations.idiomatic: In 1008, the Finance Commission said: "The treasures of mountain and marsh are won only with great difficulty; to allow them to be melted down would be sheer waste.

sentences.zh: 今約天下所用，歲不下十萬兩，俾上幣棄於下民。

translations.literal: At present the empire's annual use is no less than one hundred thousand taels, causing the sovereign's currency to be squandered among the people.
translations.idiomatic: By our estimate the empire now consumes no less than one hundred thousand taels a year, letting the sovereign's coin drain down to the populace.

sentences.zh: 自今金銀箔線，貼金、銷金、泥金、蹙金線裝貼什器土木玩用之物，並請禁斷，非命婦不得以為首飾。

translations.literal: Henceforth gold and silver foil and thread, gilt work, gold leaf, gold paste, and chased gold thread on utensils, furniture, and playthings—all are petitioned to be forbidden; only titled ladies may use gold for hair ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth gold and silver foil and thread, gilding, gold leaf, gold paste, and chased gold thread on household goods, furniture, and trinkets should all be banned, and only titled ladies may wear gold in their hair.

sentences.zh: 冶工所用器，悉送官。

translations.literal: Implements used by smelters must all be delivered to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Every implement used by smelters must be turned over to the government.

sentences.zh: 諸州寺觀有以金箔飾尊像者，據申三司，聽自齎金銀工價，就文思院換給。」

translations.literal: Temples and monasteries in the circuits that gild sacred images must report to the Finance Commission and may, bearing gold and silver and labor costs themselves, obtain supplies from the Palace Ateliers."
translations.idiomatic: Temples and monasteries that gild sacred images must report to the Finance Commission and may, at their own cost for materials and labor, obtain supplies through the Palace Ateliers."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔申禁熔金以飾器服。

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict reiterated the prohibition on melting gold to ornament vessels and dress.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an edict renewed the ban on melting gold to ornament vessels and clothing.

sentences.zh: 又太常博士知溫州李邈言：「兩浙僧求丐金銀、珠玉，錯末和泥以為塔像，有高袤丈者。

translations.literal: Also Li Miao, Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and acting prefect of Wenzhou, said: "Monks in the two Zhes beg for gold, silver, and gems, mix the filings with clay to make pagoda images some zhang in height and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Li Miao, Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and acting prefect of Wenzhou, also reported: "Monks in the two Zhes beg for gold, silver, and gems, mix the filings with clay to cast pagoda images a zhang or more in height.

sentences.zh: 毀碎珠寶，浸以成俗，望嚴行禁絕，違者重論。」

translations.literal: They grind gems to dust until it has become custom; we ask strict prohibition, with heavy penalties for violators."
translations.idiomatic: They grind precious stones to dust until it has become custom; we ask that this be strictly forbidden, with heavy punishment for offenders."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 七年，禁民間服銷金及鈸遮那纈。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, private wear of gold-leaf dress and bó-zhē-nà tie-dye was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, the people were forbidden to wear gold-leaf garments and bó-zhē-nà tie-dye.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔：「內庭自中宮以下，並不得銷金、貼金、間金、戭金、圈金、解金、剔金、陷金、明金、泥金、楞金、背影金、盤金、織金、金線拈絲，裝著衣服，並不得以金為飾。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict ordered: "Within the inner palace from the empress down, none may use gold leaf, applied gold, interlaid gold, hammered gold, ringed gold, cut gold, carved gold, inset gold, bright gold, gold paste, ribbed gold, shadow gold, coiled gold, woven gold, or gold thread twisted with silk on clothing, nor use gold as ornament at all.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year an edict declared: "From the empress down through the inner palace, no one may adorn clothing with gold leaf, applied gold, interlaid gold, hammered gold, ringed gold, cut gold, carved gold, inset gold, bright gold, gold paste, ribbed gold, shadow gold, coiled gold, woven gold, or gold thread twisted with silk, nor use gold as ornament in any form.

sentences.zh: 其外庭臣庶家，悉皆禁斷。

translations.literal: Outer-court officials and common households were all likewise forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and common households beyond the inner court were forbidden as well.

sentences.zh: 臣民舊有者，限一月許回易。

translations.literal: What officials and people already possessed was allowed one month to dispose of by exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Existing items among officials and the people had to be disposed of within one month.

sentences.zh: 為真像前供養物，應寺觀裝功德用金箔，須具殿位真像顯合增修創造數，經官司陳狀勘會，詣實聞奏，方給公憑，詣三司收買。

translations.literal: For offerings before true images and for temple merit-work using gold leaf, one must list the halls, true images, and numbers clearly fit for repair or new creation, file with officials for investigation, report truthfully to the throne, and only then receive public authorization to purchase from the Finance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings before true images and temple merit-work that use gold leaf required a full account of halls, images, and items due for repair or new creation, verification by officials, truthful report to the throne, and only then an official warrant to buy supplies from the Finance Commission.

sentences.zh: 其明金裝假果、花板、樂身之類，應金為裝彩物，降詔前已有者，更不毀壞，自餘悉禁。

translations.literal: Gilt imitation fruit, decorative panels, instrument bodies, and the like—gold-decorated objects already existing before the edict need not be destroyed; all else was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Gilt imitation fruit, decorative panels, instrument bodies, and similar gold-trimmed objects already in hand before the edict need not be destroyed; everything else was banned.

sentences.zh: 違者，犯人及工匠皆坐。」

translations.literal: Violators and craftsmen alike were prosecuted."
translations.idiomatic: Offenders and the craftsmen who served them were both punished."

sentences.zh: 是年，又禁民間服皂班纈衣。

translations.literal: That year, private wear of black barred tie-dye garments was also forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the people were also forbidden to wear black barred tie-dye.

sentences.zh: 仁宗天聖三年，詔：「在京士庶不得衣黑褐地白花衣服並藍、黃、紫地撮暈花樣，婦女不得將白色、褐色毛段並淡褐色匹帛製造衣服，令開封府限十日斷絕；

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiansheng, Emperor Renzong ordered: "Capital gentry and commoners may not wear garments of black-brown ground with white flowers, nor blue, yellow, or purple grounds with gathered halo patterns; women may not make clothes from white or brown woolens or pale-brown silks; the Kaifeng prefecture is ordered to stop this within ten days;
translations.idiomatic: In 1025, Emperor Renzong decreed: "Gentry and commoners in the capital may not wear black-brown garments patterned with white flowers, nor blue, yellow, or purple grounds with gathered halo designs; women may not make clothing from white or brown woolens or pale-brown silks; the Kaifeng prefecture must end this within ten days;

sentences.zh: 婦女出入乘騎，在路披毛褐以禦風塵者，不在禁限。」

translations.literal: Women riding out who wore woolen cloaks on the road against wind and dust were not within the prohibition."
translations.idiomatic: Women who rode out wearing woolen cloaks on the road against wind and dust were exempt."

sentences.zh: 七年，詔士庶、僧道無得以朱漆飾床榻。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict ordered that gentry, commoners, monks, and priests might not ornament bed platforms with cinnabar lacquer.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years later, gentry, commoners, monks, and priests were forbidden to lacquer bed platforms in cinnabar red.

sentences.zh: 九年，禁京城造朱紅器皿。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, making vermilion-red vessels in the capital was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the capital was forbidden to manufacture vermilion-red vessels.

sentences.zh: 景祐元年，詔禁錦背、繡背、遍地密花透背采段，其稀花團窠、斜窠雜花不相連者非。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyou, an edict forbade brocade-backed, embroidery-backed, and dense all-over openwork silks; sparse floral roundels and disconnected slanting sprays were excepted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1034, brocade-backed, embroidery-backed, and dense all-over openwork silks were banned, but sparse floral roundels and disconnected slanting sprays were not.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔：市肆造作縷金為婦人首飾等物者禁。

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict ordered: shops making filigree-gold women's hair ornaments and the like are forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: The next year shops were forbidden to make filigree-gold women's hair ornaments and similar goods.

sentences.zh: 三年，「臣庶之家，毋得采捕鹿胎製造冠子。

translations.literal: In the third year: "Common households may not hunt deer fetuses to make hats.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year: "Common households may not hunt deer fetuses to make hats.

sentences.zh: 又屋宇非邸店、樓閣臨街市之處，毋得為四鋪作鬧鬥八；

translations.literal: Also, in dwellings that are not inns or street-facing towers, four-bay decorative bracket sets to eight faces may not be built;
translations.idiomatic: Nor may dwellings that are not inns or street-facing towers build four-bay decorative bracket sets to eight faces;

sentences.zh: 非品官毋得起門屋；

translations.literal: those without official rank may not erect gate pavilions;
translations.idiomatic: those without official rank may not erect gate pavilions;

sentences.zh: 非宮室、寺觀毋得彩繪棟宇及朱黝漆梁柱窗牖、雕鏤柱礎。

translations.literal: those that are not palaces or temples may not paint buildings, lacquer pillars and windows in red or dark lacquer, or carve column bases.
translations.idiomatic: and those that are not palaces or temples may not paint their buildings, lacquer pillars and windows in red or dark lacquer, or carve column bases.

sentences.zh: 凡器用毋得表裏朱漆、金漆，下毋得襯朱。

translations.literal: All utensils may not use red lacquer inside and out or gold lacquer, nor have red lining underneath.
translations.idiomatic: No utensil may be red-lacquered inside and out or gold-lacquered, nor lined underneath in red.

sentences.zh: 非三品以上官及宗室、戚裏之家，毋得用金棱器，其用銀者毋得塗金。

translations.literal: Those below third rank, imperial clansmen, and consort kin may not use gold-rimmed vessels; silver must not be gilded.
translations.idiomatic: Households below third rank, imperial clansmen, and consort kin may not use gold-rimmed vessels, and silver must not be gilded.

sentences.zh: 玳瑁酒食器，非宮禁毋得用。

translations.literal: Tortoiseshell food and drink vessels may be used only within the palace precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Tortoiseshell food and drink vessels were reserved for the palace.

sentences.zh: 純金器若經賜者，聽用之。

translations.literal: Pure gold vessels, if bestowed by imperial gift, may be used.
translations.idiomatic: Pure gold vessels might be used if the emperor had bestowed them.

sentences.zh: 凡命婦許以金為首飾，及為小兒鈐鋜、釵篸、钅川纏、珥環之屬；

translations.literal: Titled ladies were permitted to use gold for hair ornaments and for children's clasps, hairpins, armlets, and ear rings and the like;
translations.idiomatic: Titled ladies might wear gold in their hair and give children gold clasps, hairpins, armlets, and earrings;

sentences.zh: 仍毋得為牙魚、飛魚、奇巧飛動若龍形者。

translations.literal: but they might not take the forms of ivory fish, flying fish, clever flying things, or dragon shapes.
translations.idiomatic: but not in the shapes of ivory fish, flying fish, clever flying forms, or dragons.

sentences.zh: 非命婦之家，毋得以真珠裝綴首飾、衣服，及項珠、纓絡、耳墜、頭{須巾}、抹子之類。

translations.literal: Households without titled ladies may not use pearls to trim hair ornaments and clothing, nor neck pearls, tassels, ear pendants, head-bands, forehead cloths, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Households without titled ladies might not trim hair ornaments or clothing with pearls, nor wear neck pearls, tassels, ear pendants, head-bands, forehead cloths, and the like.

sentences.zh: 凡帳幔、繳壁、承塵、柱衣、額道、項帕、覆旌、床裙，毋得用純錦遍繡。

translations.literal: Curtains, wall hangings, valances, pillar wraps, friezes, neck cloths, coverlets, and bed skirts may not use pure brocade with all-over embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: Curtains, wall hangings, valances, pillar wraps, friezes, neck cloths, coverlets, and bed skirts might not be made of brocade embroidered throughout.

sentences.zh: 宗室戚裏茶簷、食合，毋得以緋紅蓋覆。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen and consort kin may not cover tea trays and food boxes with scarlet cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial kinsmen and consort kin might not cover tea trays and food boxes with scarlet cloth.

sentences.zh: 豪貴之族所乘坐車，毋得用朱漆及五彩裝繪，若用黝而間以五彩者聽。

translations.literal: Carriages ridden by wealthy noble families may not use red lacquer or five-color painting; if dark lacquer is used with five-color accents interspersed, it is permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Carriages of the wealthy elite might not be red-lacquered or painted in five colors, though dark lacquer with five-color accents was allowed.

sentences.zh: 民間毋得乘簷子，及以銀骨朵、水罐引喝隨行。」

translations.literal: Among the people, riding sedan chairs and following with silver maces and water jars to clear the way are forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: Commoners might not ride sedan chairs or parade with silver maces and water jars to clear the road."

sentences.zh: 慶曆八年，詔禁士庶效契丹服及乘騎鞍轡、婦人衣銅綠兔褐之類。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Qingli, an edict forbade gentry and commoners from imitating Khitan dress, saddlery, and women from wearing copper-green rabbit-fur coats and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In 1048, gentry and commoners were forbidden to imitate Khitan dress and saddlery, and women were forbidden copper-green rabbit-fur coats and the like.

sentences.zh: 皇祐元年，詔婦人冠高毋得逾四寸，廣毋得逾尺，梳長毋得逾四寸，仍禁以角為之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangyou, an edict ordered that women's crowns be no more than four cun high and one chi wide, combs no more than four cun long, and horn was still forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In 1049, women's crowns were capped at four cun in height and one chi in width, combs at four cun in length, and horn was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 先是，宮中尚白角冠梳，人爭仿之，至謂之內樣。

translations.literal: Previously the palace had favored white horn crowns and combs; people competed to imitate them, even calling them "inner-court style."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the palace had favored white horn crowns and combs, and people rushed to copy them until they called the fashion "inner-court style."

sentences.zh: 冠名曰垂肩等肩，至有長三尺者；

translations.literal: Crowns named "draping-shoulder" and "level-shoulder" reached as much as three chi in length;
translations.idiomatic: Crowns called "draping-shoulder" and "level-shoulder" grew as long as three chi;

sentences.zh: 梳長亦逾尺。

translations.literal: combs also exceeded one chi in length.
translations.idiomatic: and combs too grew longer than a foot.

sentences.zh: 議者以為服妖，遂禁止之。

translations.literal: Critics deemed it prodigious dress, and it was therefore forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Critics called it a dress of ill omen, and it was banned.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐七年，初，皇親與內臣所衣紫，皆再入為黝色。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiayou, at first the purple worn by imperial kinsmen and inner attendants was dyed a second time to a dark tone.
translations.idiomatic: In 1062, imperial kinsmen and inner attendants had their purple garments dyed a second time to a dark hue.

sentences.zh: 後士庶浸相效，言者以為奇邪之服，於是禁天下衣黑紫服者。

translations.literal: Later gentry and commoners gradually imitated one another; memorialists called it heterodox dress, and black-purple clothing was then forbidden throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Later gentry and commoners imitated them in turn; memorialists called it outlandish dress, and black-purple clothing was banned empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 神宗熙寧九年，禁朝服紫色近黑者；

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xining, Emperor Shenzong forbade court dress in purple near black;
translations.idiomatic: In 1076, Emperor Shenzong forbade court dress in purple so dark it was nearly black;

sentences.zh: 民庶止令乘犢車，聽以黑飾，間五彩為飾，不許嗬引及前列儀物。

translations.literal: common people were allowed only ox-carts, with black trim permitted and five-color accents interspersed as ornament; shouting escorts and front ceremonial display were not allowed.
translations.idiomatic: commoners were limited to ox-carts with black trim and touches of five-color ornament, but not shouting escorts or front ceremonial display.

sentences.zh: 哲宗紹聖二年，侍御史翟思言：「京城士人與豪右大姓，出入率以轎自載，四人舁之，甚者飾以棕蓋，徹去簾蔽，翼其左右，旁午於通衢，甚為僭擬，乞行止絕。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaosheng, Censor Zhai Si said: "Capital scholars and great wealthy clans routinely go out in enclosed chairs borne by four men; some even ornament them with palm-leaf canopies, remove the curtains, and flank them left and right, crisscrossing the main thoroughfares—great usurpation of rank; I petition that this be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: In 1095, Censor Zhai Si said: "Scholars and great families in the capital routinely travel in enclosed chairs borne by four men; some even add palm-leaf canopies, strip away the curtains, and flank themselves on both sides, crisscrossing the main roads in brazen imitation of rank. I ask that this be stopped."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 七年，臣僚上言：「輦轂之下，奔競侈靡，有未革者。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, officials memorialized: "Under the imperial axle-tree, rivalry in extravagance still has unreformed aspects.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years later officials memorialized: "Beneath the imperial chariot-axle, rivalry in luxury still has unreformed aspects.

sentences.zh: 居室服用以壯麗相誇，珠璣金玉以奇巧相勝，不獨貴近，比比紛紛，日益滋甚。

translations.literal: Dwellings and dress compete in splendor; pearls, gems, and gold compete in novelty—not only the noble and near, but everywhere, growing worse day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Homes and dress are judged by splendor, pearls and gold by novelty—not only the high and near, but everywhere, and growing worse by the day.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗考之，申令法禁雖具，其罰尚輕，有司玩習，以至於此。

translations.literal: Your servant has examined the matter: though proclamations and legal prohibitions exist, the penalties remain light and officials treat them lightly, leading to this.
translations.idiomatic: I have looked into it: though the laws and bans are on the books, the penalties are still light and officials treat them casually, which is how we have come to this.

sentences.zh: 如民庶之家不得乘轎，今京城內暖轎，非命官至富民、娼優、下賤，遂以為常。

translations.literal: For example, common households may not ride enclosed chairs, yet in the capital today heated enclosed chairs—from titled ladies to the wealthy, entertainers, and the base—have become routine.
translations.idiomatic: Common households, for instance, may not ride enclosed chairs, yet in the capital heated enclosed chairs are now routine for everyone from titled ladies to the wealthy, courtesans, and the lowborn.

sentences.zh: 竊見近日有赴內禁乘以至皇城門者，奉祀乘至宮廟者，坦然無所畏避。

translations.literal: I have lately seen some ride them to the inner palace gates for audiences and to palace temples for sacrifices, openly without fear.
translations.idiomatic: Lately I have even seen people ride them to the inner palace gates for audiences and to palace temples for sacrifices, openly and without fear.

sentences.zh: 臣妄以為僭禮犯分，禁亦不可以緩。」

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to deem this usurpation of ritual and violation of rank; prohibition also cannot be relaxed."
translations.idiomatic: I take this to be usurpation of ritual and violation of rank, and the ban cannot be relaxed."

sentences.zh: 於是詔，非品官不得乘暖轎。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered that only ranked officials might ride heated enclosed chairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: only ranked officials might ride heated enclosed chairs.

sentences.zh: 先是，權發遣提舉淮南東路學事丁瓘言：「衣服之制，尤不可緩。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ding Jin, acting education intendant for Huainan East Circuit, had said: "Regulations on clothing especially cannot be neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ding Jin, acting education intendant for Huainan East Circuit, had said: "Dress regulations above all cannot be neglected.

sentences.zh: 今閭閻之卑，倡優之賤，男子服帶犀玉，婦人塗飾金珠，尚多僭侈，未合古制。

translations.literal: Today in low alleys and among base entertainers, men belt themselves with rhinoceros horn and jade and women paint themselves in gold and pearls—much still exceeds proper rank and does not accord with ancient regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Today in the lowest lanes and among entertainers, men belt themselves with rhinoceros horn and jade and women paint themselves in gold and pearls—far too much extravagance, and out of keeping with ancient rule.

sentences.zh: 臣恐禮官所議，止正大典，未遑及此。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that what the ritual officials discuss will rectify only the great statutes and will not reach this.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the ritual officials will fix only the great statutes and never reach this.

sentences.zh: 伏願明詔有司，嚴立法度，酌古便今，以義起禮。

translations.literal: I humbly wish a clear edict to the responsible offices to establish strict law, weighing antiquity and convenience for today, founding ritual in righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask for a clear edict to the responsible offices to set strict law, weighing antiquity against present need and founding ritual in righteousness.

sentences.zh: 俾閭閻之卑，不得與尊者同榮；

translations.literal: So that the low alleys may not share glory with the honored;
translations.idiomatic: Let the lowest lanes not share in the glory of the honored;

sentences.zh: 倡優之賤，不得與貴者並麗。

translations.literal: nor base entertainers share beauty with the exalted.
translations.idiomatic: nor entertainers share splendor with the exalted.

sentences.zh: 此法一正，名分自明，革澆偷以歸忠厚，豈曰小補之哉。」

translations.literal: Once this law is set right, names and ranks clarify themselves; reforming indulgence returns to steadfastness—how could it be called a small benefit?"
translations.idiomatic: Once this law is set right, names and ranks will clarify themselves, indulgence will give way to steadfastness, and the gain will be no small one."

sentences.zh: 是歲，又詔敢為契丹服若氈笠、釣墩之類者，以違御筆論。

translations.literal: That year, another edict ordered that those daring to wear Khitan dress such as felt caps and diaodun would be punished as defying the emperor's brush.
translations.idiomatic: That year another edict declared that anyone daring to wear Khitan dress such as felt caps or diaodun would be punished for defying the emperor's own brush.

sentences.zh: 釣墩，今亦謂之襪袴，婦人之服也。

translations.literal: Diaodun—now also called sock-trousers—is women's dress.
translations.idiomatic: Diaodun, now also called sock-trousers, is women's dress.

sentences.zh: 中興，士大夫之服，大抵因東都之舊，而其後稍變焉。

translations.literal: After the restoration, scholar-official dress largely followed the Eastern Capital tradition, and afterward changed somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration, the dress of scholar-officials largely followed Eastern Capital custom, then shifted gradually.

sentences.zh: 一曰深衣，二曰紫衫，三曰涼衫，四曰帽衫，五曰襴衫。

translations.literal: First, deep robes; second, purple jackets; third, cool jackets; fourth, cap jackets; fifth, barred jackets.
translations.idiomatic: There were five kinds: deep robes, purple jackets, cool jackets, cap jackets, and barred jackets.

sentences.zh: 淳熙中，朱熹又定祭祀、冠婚之服，特頒行之。

translations.literal: In the Chunxi era Zhu Xi again fixed sacrificial and capping-wedding dress, which was specially promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunxi era Zhu Xi set dress for sacrifice and for capping and wedding rites, and it was specially promulgated.

sentences.zh: 凡士大夫家祭祀、冠婚，則具盛服。

translations.literal: Whenever scholar-official families performed sacrifice or capping-wedding rites, they prepared full ceremonial dress.
translations.idiomatic: For sacrifice, capping, or marriage, scholar-official families prepared full ceremonial dress.

sentences.zh: 有官者襆頭、帶、靴、笏，進士則襆頭、襴衫、帶，處士則襆頭、皂衫、帶，無官者通用帽子、衫、帶；

translations.literal: Officials wore futou, belt, boots, and tablet; jinshi wore futou, barred jacket, and belt; retired scholars wore futou, black jacket, and belt; those without office generally wore hat, jacket, and belt;
translations.idiomatic: Officeholders wore futou, belt, boots, and tablet; jinshi wore futou, barred jacket, and belt; retired scholars wore futou, black jacket, and belt; men without office generally wore hat, jacket, and belt;

sentences.zh: 又不能具，則或深衣，或涼衫。

translations.literal: if they could not assemble these, then either deep robes or cool jackets.
translations.idiomatic: if they could not manage the full set, they might wear deep robes or cool jackets instead.

sentences.zh: 有官者亦通用帽子以下，但不為盛服。

translations.literal: Officials might also generally use hat and below, but this was not full ceremonial dress.
translations.idiomatic: Officeholders might also wear hat and the like, but that did not count as full ceremonial dress.

sentences.zh: 婦人則假髻、大衣、長裙。

translations.literal: Women wore false topknots, great coats, and long skirts.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore false topknots, great coats, and long skirts.

sentences.zh: 女子在室者冠子、背子。

translations.literal: Unmarried girls wore coronets and over-jackets.
translations.idiomatic: Unmarried girls wore coronets and over-jackets.

sentences.zh: 眾妾則假紒、背子。

translations.literal: Concubines wore false braided coils and over-jackets.
translations.idiomatic: Concubines wore false braided coils and over-jackets.

sentences.zh: 冠禮，三加冠服，初加，緇布冠、深衣、大帶、納履；

translations.literal: For the capping rite, three investitures of crown and dress: at the first, black cloth cap, deep robes, great belt, and slip-on shoes;
translations.idiomatic: In the capping rite there were three investitures: first, black cloth cap, deep robes, great belt, and slip-on shoes;

sentences.zh: 再加，帽子、皂衫、革帶、係鞋；

translations.literal: at the second, hat, black jacket, leather belt, and laced shoes;
translations.idiomatic: second, hat, black jacket, leather belt, and laced shoes;

sentences.zh: 三加，襆頭、公服、革帶、納靴。

translations.literal: at the third, futou, public dress, leather belt, and fastened boots.
translations.idiomatic: third, futou, public dress, leather belt, and fastened boots.

sentences.zh: 其品官嫡庶子初加，折上巾、公服；

translations.literal: For ranked officials' legitimate and secondary sons at the first investiture, folded-up cap and public dress;
translations.idiomatic: For the sons of ranked officials, legitimate and secondary alike, the first investiture was folded-up cap and public dress;

sentences.zh: 再加，二梁冠、朝服；

translations.literal: at the second, two-ridge cap and court dress;
translations.idiomatic: second, two-ridge cap and court dress;

sentences.zh: 三加，平冕服，若以巾帽、折上巾為三加者，聽之。

translations.literal: at the third, plain coronet dress; if cap-and-hat or folded-up cap serve as the third investiture, that is permitted.
translations.idiomatic: third, plain coronet dress; one might instead use cap-and-hat or folded-up cap for the third investiture if desired.

sentences.zh: 深衣用白細布，度用指尺，衣全四幅，其長過脅，下屬於裳。

translations.literal: Deep robes used fine white cloth; measurements used finger-cubits; the upper garment was fully four panels, its length passing the ribs, and below it was joined to the skirt.
translations.idiomatic: Deep robes were made of fine white cloth, measured with finger-cubits; the upper garment had four full panels, long enough to pass the ribs, and was joined below to the skirt.

sentences.zh: 裳交解十二幅，上屬於衣，其長及踝。

translations.literal: The skirt crossed and parted in twelve panels, joined above to the garment, its length reaching the ankle.
translations.idiomatic: The skirt had twelve cross-cut panels, attached above to the garment, and fell to the ankle.

sentences.zh: 圓袂方領，曲裾黑緣。

translations.literal: Round sleeves, square collar, curved hem with black border.
translations.idiomatic: They had round sleeves and a square collar, with a curved hem bordered in black.

sentences.zh: 大帶、緇冠、幅巾、黑履。

translations.literal: Great belt, black cap, cloth headwrap, and black shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Accessories were the great belt, black cap, cloth headwrap, and black shoes.

sentences.zh: 士大夫家冠昏、祭祀、宴居、交際服之。

translations.literal: Scholar-official families wore them for capping and marriage, sacrifice, leisure at home, and social exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-official families wore them for capping and marriage, sacrifice, everyday leisure, and social occasions.

sentences.zh: 紫衫。

translations.literal: Purple jackets.
translations.idiomatic: Purple jackets.

sentences.zh: 本軍校服。

translations.literal: Originally army school dress.
translations.idiomatic: Originally this was dress of the army schools.

sentences.zh: 中興，士大夫服之，以便戎事。

translations.literal: After the restoration, scholar-officials wore them to suit military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration scholar-officials adopted them for convenience in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 紹興九年，詔公卿、長吏服用冠帶，然迄不行。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shaoxing an edict ordered dukes, ministers, and chief officials to wear caps and belts, but in the end it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 9 an edict required grandees and chief officials to wear caps and belts, but the order never took effect.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，再申嚴禁，毋得以戎服臨民，自是紫衫遂廢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the prohibition was reaffirmed in strict terms: one must not approach the people in military dress; thereafter purple jackets were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 the ban was enforced again: officials might not receive the people in military dress, and purple jackets fell out of use.

sentences.zh: 士大夫皆服涼衫，以為便服矣。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials all wore cool jackets, taking them as convenient dress.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials all switched to cool jackets as everyday wear.

sentences.zh: 涼衫。

translations.literal: Cool jackets.
translations.idiomatic: Cool jackets.

sentences.zh: 其制如紫衫，亦曰白衫。

translations.literal: Their form was like purple jackets; they were also called white jackets.
translations.idiomatic: Cut like purple jackets, they were also known as white jackets.

sentences.zh: 乾道初，禮部侍郎王嚴奏：「竊見近日士大夫皆服涼衫，甚非美觀，而以交際、居官、臨民，純素可憎，有似凶服。

translations.literal: Early in Qiandao, Vice Minister of Rites Wang Yan memorialized: "I have observed that recently scholar-officials all wear cool jackets, which is quite unsightly; yet they use them in social exchange, in holding office, and in receiving the people. Plain white is repugnant and resembles mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiandao, Wang Yan, Vice Minister of Rites, wrote: "Lately every scholar-official seems to wear cool jackets. They are unseemly, yet people wear them when mingling, holding office, or dealing with the public—plain white that offends the eye and looks like mourning.

sentences.zh: 陛下方奉兩宮，所宜革之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is just now serving the two palaces; this ought to be reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is still caring for the retired sovereigns of the two palaces; such dress ought to be abolished.

sentences.zh: 且紫衫之設以從戎，故為之禁，而人情趨簡便，靡而至此。

translations.literal: Moreover purple jackets were established to follow the army, hence the prohibition was made; yet human inclination trends toward simplicity, and excess has reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Purple jackets were meant for military service, which is why they were restricted; but people prefer what is easy, and indulgence has brought us here.

sentences.zh: 文武並用。

translations.literal: Civil and military alike used them.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials alike wore them.

sentences.zh: 本不偏廢，朝章之外，宜有便衣，仍存紫衫，未害大體。」

translations.literal: They were not meant to be wholly abolished; outside court regalia there should be convenient dress, and purple jackets might remain—this would not harm the larger principle."
translations.idiomatic: The aim was not to abolish them entirely: beyond court regalia one needs informal dress, and keeping purple jackets would not undermine proper order."

sentences.zh: 於是禁服白衫，除乘馬道塗許服外，餘不得服。

translations.literal: Thereupon white jackets were prohibited; except when riding on horseback on the road one might wear them—otherwise they might not be worn.
translations.idiomatic: White jackets were then banned except when riding on public roads; otherwise they could not be worn.

sentences.zh: 若便服，許用紫衫。

translations.literal: For convenient dress, purple jackets were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: For informal wear, purple jackets were allowed.

sentences.zh: 自後，涼衫祗用為凶服矣。

translations.literal: Afterward cool jackets were used only as mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: After that, cool jackets served only as mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 帽衫。

translations.literal: Cap jackets.
translations.idiomatic: Cap jackets.

sentences.zh: 帽以烏紗、衫以皂羅為之，角帶，係鞋。

translations.literal: The cap was of black gauze and the jacket of black gauze silk; horn belt and laced shoes.
translations.idiomatic: The cap was black gauze and the jacket black silk gauze, with horn belt and laced shoes.

sentences.zh: 東都時，士大夫交際常服之。

translations.literal: In Eastern Capital times scholar-officials commonly wore them in social exchange.
translations.idiomatic: In the Eastern Capital era scholar-officials wore them regularly in daily social life.

sentences.zh: 南渡後，一變為紫衫，再變為涼衫，自是服帽衫少矣。

translations.literal: After the southward crossing, first they changed to purple jackets, then again to cool jackets; from then on cap jackets were worn less.
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved south they gave way first to purple jackets, then to cool jackets, and cap jackets became rare.

sentences.zh: 惟士大夫家冠昏、祭祀猶服焉。

translations.literal: Only in scholar-official families' capping and marriage and sacrifice were they still worn.
translations.idiomatic: Only for capping, marriage, and sacrifice in scholar-official households did people still wear them.

sentences.zh: 若國子生，常服之。

translations.literal: Imperial University students wore them as regular dress.
translations.idiomatic: Students of the Imperial University wore them as daily dress.

sentences.zh: 襴衫。

translations.literal: Barred jackets.
translations.idiomatic: Barred jackets.

sentences.zh: 以白細布為之，圓領大袖，下施橫襴為裳，腰間有辟積。

translations.literal: Made of fine white cloth, round collar and large sleeves; below, horizontal bars served as the skirt, with pleats at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: They were fine white cloth, round-collared and large-sleeved, with horizontal barred panels below like a skirt and pleats at the waist.

sentences.zh: 進士及國子生、州縣生服之。

translations.literal: Jinshi, Imperial University students, and prefectural and county students wore them.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi candidates, Imperial University students, and local academy students wore them.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年，高宗謂輔臣曰：「金翠為婦人服飾，不惟靡貨害物，而侈靡之習，實關風化。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxing Emperor Gaozong said to his chief ministers: "Gold and kingfisher feather as women's adornment not only wastes goods and harms creatures, but the habit of extravagance truly bears on moral transformation.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 5 Gaozong told his chief ministers: "Women's ornaments of gold and kingfisher feather waste wealth, harm living things, and—more importantly—extravagant habits bear directly on public morals.

sentences.zh: 已戒中外，及下令不許入宮門，今無一人犯者。

translations.literal: I have already admonished court and countryside, and ordered that none may enter the palace gates wearing them; now not a single person has violated this.
translations.idiomatic: I have warned the court and the provinces and barred such dress from the palace gates; not one person has violated the order since.

sentences.zh: 尚恐士民之家未能盡革，宜申嚴禁，仍定銷金及采捕金翠罪賞格。」

translations.literal: I still fear that scholar and common households may not have reformed entirely; the strict prohibition should be reaffirmed, and scales of crime and reward set for gilding gold and for collecting and catching gold and kingfisher materials."
translations.idiomatic: I fear gentry and common households may not have reformed fully; tighten the prohibition and fix penalties and rewards for gilding and for hunting kingfisher or mining its materials."

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年，孝宗宣示中宮禕衣曰：「珠玉就用禁中舊物，所費不及五萬，革弊當自宮禁始。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunxi Emperor Xiaozong displayed the empress's formal sacrificial robes and said: "Pearls and jade use old items from within the Forbidden City; the cost does not reach fifty thousand; reforming abuses ought to begin within the palace confines."
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi 2 Xiaozong showed the empress's sacrificial robe and said: "Use pearls and jade already in the palace—under fifty thousand in cost. Reform must begin inside the palace itself."

sentences.zh: 因問風俗，龔茂良奏：「由貴近之家，放效宮禁，以致流傳民間。

translations.literal: He then asked about customs; Gong Maoliang reported: "It starts with eminent and close families imitating the palace, until it spreads among the people.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked about popular customs. Gong Maoliang replied: "Eminent families near the throne copy palace styles, and the fashion spreads to the people.

sentences.zh: 粥簪珥者，必言內樣。

translations.literal: Those who sell hairpins and earrings invariably say 'inner-court style.'
translations.idiomatic: Vendors of hairpins and earrings always advertise 'as worn inside.'

sentences.zh: 彼若知上崇尚淳樸，必觀感而化矣。

translations.literal: If they knew the sovereign esteems plain simplicity, they would surely be moved by seeing and reform.
translations.idiomatic: If they knew the throne valued simplicity, they would be moved to reform by the example alone.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞中宮服浣濯之衣，數年不易。

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that within the palace they wear washed clothes, not changed for several years.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that consorts in the palace wear washed garments for years without replacing them.

sentences.zh: 請宣示中外，仍敕有司嚴戢奢僭。」

translations.literal: I ask that this be displayed to court and countryside, and that the responsible offices be ordered to curb extravagance and usurpation strictly."
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim this within the court and without, and order officials to suppress extravagance and presumptuous display."

sentences.zh: 寧宗嘉泰初，以風俗侈靡，詔官民營建室屋，一遵制度，務從簡樸。

translations.literal: Early in Jiatai under Emperor Ningzong, because customs were extravagant, an edict ordered officials and people building houses to follow regulations entirely and aim at simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiatai, finding customs extravagant, Ningzong ordered officials and commoners alike to build houses strictly by regulation and keep them plain.

sentences.zh: 又以宮中金翠，燔之通衢，貴近之家，犯者必罰。

translations.literal: Palace gold and kingfisher were also burned in the public thoroughfare; for eminent and close families, violators were certainly punished.
translations.idiomatic: Gold and kingfisher ornaments from the palace were burned in the public streets, and eminent families who violated the rules were punished without exception.
